findings.topic: SC09 spline geometry from the official STEP
findings.finding: From the downloaded files.waveshare.com/upload/9/9f/SC09.zip, SC09-SERVO.step, measured with build123d: 20 teeth, OD 3.95, root Ø3.45 (tooth height 0.25 mm). Toothed length 2.21 mm plus a 0.29 mm chamfer down to Ø3.0 at the tip. A plain Ø4.0 collar about 0.8 mm long sits under the teeth. Centre hole Ø1.6, 5.0 mm deep. Ø1.6 is the M2 tap-drill size, but the thread is not modelled, so M2 is assumed and unverified. The axis is 5.7 mm from the case end. Official drawing: spline protrudes 3.2 above the top face (2.9 also marked), 25.25 to the top face, 28.45 overall.

Seeed SCS0009 datasheet (via search): 'SCS0009 Servo x1, Servo Horn x3, Screw x3, JST Wire x1, JST Board x1'. The Waveshare SC09 page lists Package Content as 'SC09 Servo x1' only. Its product photo 5 nevertheless shows white plastic horns (cross, round disc, double arm, single arm), 3 small screws (2 longer, 1 short), a cable and an adapter board. Box contents may therefore differ by seller. Screw thread sizes and lengths are not published anywhere I could reach.

findings.topic: Horn dimensions from the official horn STEP
findings.finding: From SC09-ARM.step (Waveshare, measured): single-arm horn hub Ø7.4, height 4.1, reaches 17.2 mm from the axis. Double-arm horn hub Ø6.9, height 3.7, total length 31.35. Cross horn 16.5 x 33.7, height 3.8. Arm holes Ø1.0 at about 2.0 mm pitch. Centre screw hole Ø2.5-2.75 with a Ø4.5-5.4 counterbore. The older sc09.zip adds a disc Ø24 x 4.1 and a 34.6 mm double arm. The horn's internal spline is modelled as 20T Ø4.2/Ø4.8 over 2.35 mm, which does NOT match the servo's OD 3.95, so it is a simplified model. Do not copy it for a printed spline; use the servo STEP.

findings.topic: How hobbyists couple printed parts to a servo spline
findings.finding: The consistent advice is to glue the servo's own horn into a printed recess rather than print the spline: 'The horn gets glued into the printed part. Press on the horn, not on your 3D part. It can take quite a bit of force to get the horn onto the spline' (Instructables). Printing the spline directly is reported as unreliable because spline sizes vary between batches by about 0.2 mm. Melting the spline in with a soldering iron only works for thermoplastics, not for cured resin.

findings.topic: Elegoo Tough resin mechanical data (no official TDS reachable)
findings.finding: Amazon.de listing for the original grey Tough resin: tensile 32.12 MPa ±10 %, bending strength 35.13 MPa ±10 %, elongation at break 43.76 %, Shore D 78-81. Another Amazon listing gives flexural strength 45.116 MPa. Tough 2.0 listing: tensile 28.69 MPa, elongation 55.15 %, Shore D 80-85. Reseller diy3d.in: ~46 MPa tensile, ~25 % elongation, ~85D. No HDT is published for Elegoo Tough; ABS-Like 3.0+ is about 55 °C. The numbers are inconsistent between versions, so the project's 8.5 MPa allowable is about 26 % of the 32 MPa tensile value.

Formlabs Tough 1000: UTS 26.3 MPa, sold as 'low friction, lubricity comparable to Delrin', for hinges and gears, with 'long-term fatigue resistance' (qualitative only; no S-N curve published). Raise3D Tough 2K: 45 MPa tensile, 35 % elongation, E 2158 MPa, flexural 90 MPa, HDT 68 °C at 0.45 MPa. Generic tough-resin range (Craftcloud): 33-60 MPa tensile, 11-51 % elongation, HDT 50-70 °C. No published fatigue or creep data for tough photopolymers was found.

Hackaday 2022: a resin 80:1 compound planetary gearbox failed early. After a reprint in a stronger resin it ran past 500 cycles, then failed with 'broken teeth and powdered resin', while the PLA version showed little wear. Jan Mrázek (CZ) found that the filled composite resin Siraya Fast Mecha showed no visible tooth wear in a 1:85 planetary test to failure. His Tenacious-mix gearbox transmitted 4.6 N.m with no grinding residue. Formlabs forum: 'small fine tooth internal gears won't be very durable with pretty much any printed material'. No controlled wear data exists for m0.5 MSLA gears in Elegoo Tough.

Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K: 15120 x 6230 LCD, XY pixel 14 x 19 µm (Elegoo/Hackster/Fabbaloo). An m0.5 tooth is 1.125 mm high (about 59-80 px) and the 20T servo spline tooth is 0.25 mm high (about 13-18 px), so resolution is not the limit; fit and shrinkage are. A Formlabs Tough hole/shaft test (2017) gave a clearance fit at ≥0.05 mm allowance, a hand-push transition at 0-0.0375 mm, and press-only at -0.0375 mm. These values are for Formlabs, not Elegoo, so use a test coupon.

findings.topic: Printed bevel pair strength (own Lewis calc, project numbers)
findings.finding: Lewis bending, bevel (virtual teeth, mean module), Elegoo Tough, Kv 1. Script: /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/prieskum_tlacene/gear_lewis.py, results in gear_lewis.json. For K3 m0.5 16/24, b 2.4, cone distance R 7.21, the pinion root stress is 2.5 MPa at the 0.004 N.m arm load, 27 MPa at the 15 % homing limit (0.043 N.m at the arm) and 38 MPa at the 0.06 N.m clutch. That pair reaches 8.5 MPa at only 0.0134 N.m and the 32 MPa tensile value at about 0.051 N.m. Other module choices in the same envelope barely help: m0.6 13/20 gives 0.0149, m0.75 11/16 gives 0.0171 and m0.8 10/15 gives 0.0167 N.m at 8.5 MPa. A larger pair (m0.6 16/24, d 9.6/14.4) gives 0.0233. The 16/16 miter fallback gives only 0.0084. Conclusion: with printed gears, the clutch and homing torques must drop below about 0.012 N.m; otherwise the teeth break at the current settings.

No MSLA-specific bevel-gear orientation study was found. General guidance: flat orientation (axis vertical, teeth profiles in the XY plane) gives the best tooth-profile accuracy, but layers then run across the tooth root (Sovol). An AmeraLabs MSLA linear-gear case printed the teeth on the build plate and reached about 50 µm accuracy. A Formlabs user found small gears came out clean only when printed horizontally. For a bevel gear, axis-vertical printing with supports on the back face or hub (never on the flanks) is the usual choice, but this is unverified.

Formlabs forum thread 'Resin on Resin lubricant?': 'Graphite works very well' (dry graphite cannot soak in); 'Silicone lubes make things sticky'; 'SuperLube seems to dissolve the surface of white resin' (one anecdote; another user says Super Lube works). Another forum user says lithium or mineral grease is fine on plastics. Guidance for thermoplastics: silicone and PTFE greases are inert, while soap greases with mineral oil can cause stress cracking (not proven for photopolymers). No manufacturer statement on grease compatibility for Elegoo Tough was found, so test on a scrap print for several days.

No test data was found for printed photopolymer bushings on steel. BU SLA tolerance guide: 'for kinetic assemblies that need to last for many motion cycles without wear, it is best to use off-the-shelf Delrin bushings embedded in Tough Resin parts.' igus data for comparison: the shaft finish (about Ra 0.1-0.2 µm, ground) and hardness dominate wear; both too smooth and too rough a shaft increase wear. A screw thread is a file, so resin must never slide on a thread.

ISO 4762 / DIN 912 reference thread length for M3 is b = 18 mm. An M3x30 would then have about 12 mm of plain shank and an M3x35 about 17 mm (my inference from b, not a sourced row). Cheap hobby-store 'DIN 912' screws are often fully threaded, so a plain shank cannot be counted on. Shoulder screws (ISO 7379) did not turn up in any common shop.

common_parts.item: Servo horns + screws for SCS0009 / SC09 (20T, OD 3.95)
common_parts.sizes_commonly_stocked: Supplied with the servo: cross, disc, double-arm and single-arm horns (white plastic), 3 screws
common_parts.shops: In the box per the Seeed datasheet ('Servo Horn x3, Screw x3'); Waveshare photo shows 4 horns + 3 screws (https://www.waveshare.com/sc09-servo.htm)
common_parts.notes: Waveshare's package list says 'SC09 Servo x1' only, so check the box. Spare 20T/3.95 horns were not found as a separate common item. Screw size is unpublished; the spline hole is Ø1.6 x 5.0 deep (M2 assumed).

recommendations: Gear load is the main risk. A printed Elegoo Tough m0.5 16/24 bevel pair reaches the 8.5 MPa allowable at about 0.013 N.m at the arm and the tensile strength at about 0.05 N.m, so the current 0.06 N.m clutch and the 0.043 N.m homing limit would break it. Set the clutch slip to about 0.010 N.m (2.5x the 0.004 N.m the arm needs; pinion stress about 6.3 MPa). Keep the homing and stall torque below the clutch, i.e. at most about 2.5-3 % of servo torque (unverified that the SCS0009 torque limit goes that low). Changing the module in the same envelope gains less than 30 %; only a larger pair (e.g. m0.6 16/24, d 9.6/14.4: 0.023 N.m) or lower torque helps. Do not use the 16/16 miter fallback in resin (0.008 N.m).

Treat printed-gear life and noise as unverified. Published evidence is anecdotal: resin gearboxes powdered and broke while a filled resin (Fast Mecha) survived. Print a test pair, run it about 10^4 to 10^5 cycles at the 0.010 N.m clutch torque with the chosen lubricant, and measure backlash before committing.

Servo coupling without metal work: do not rely on a printed 20T internal spline. Trim a supplied plastic horn with side cutters and file two flats on its hub (plastic, so allowed). Bond it with 2K epoxy into a printed coupler pocket of matching shape, so torque goes through the shape and not only the glue. Press it onto the spline by the horn, not the print. Retain it with the supplied centre screw (spline hole Ø1.6 x 5.0 deep, M2 assumed); the screw must not bottom out (Waveshare FAQ warns about screws touching the servo). A printed spline (20T, OD 3.95, root 3.45, about 2.2 mm toothed) is only a fallback, made from a test coupon with radial offsets of 0 / +0.02 / +0.04 / +0.06 mm.

Bearings: keep MR63ZZ, MR74ZZ and 6700ZZ. All three come from one common 3D-printing source (Bambu Lab EU store: micro 6-packs EA006/EA009, 6700ZZ 2-pack EA032), with RC shops (3x6x2.5, 4x7x2.5, 10x15x4) and tymoty.com / loziska-policka.cz as backups. 623ZZ, 624ZZ, 625ZZ, 688ZZ, 608ZZ, 6701ZZ and MR105ZZ are also safe choices. Avoid MR83, MR85, MR93, MR115, MR128, 683, 684, 6800 and 61800 (specialist only).

Shafts from screws: use a screw only as a static axle bonded into resin (thread in epoxy or Loctite in a printed bore), and let ball bearings carry the rotation. Never let resin slide on a thread. Do not count on a plain shank in hobby-store DIN 912 screws (often fully threaded; ISO M3 b = 18 mm). Where a bearing must sit on a screw, put it on a printed sleeve or seat, not on the thread.

Printed plain bushings: only for slow, light, intermittent motion. Use a resin-on-steel clearance of about 0.05-0.10 mm (Formlabs Tough data: ≥0.05 mm gives a clearance fit), verified by a coupon on the user's printer. For many cycles, prefer the ball bearings above.

Lubrication: forum evidence favours dry graphite for resin-on-resin contact. Silicone can become sticky, and one user saw SuperLube attack white resin. If grease is used on the gear mesh, put a dab of the chosen grease on a cured Elegoo Tough scrap for 3-7 days and check for softening, tackiness or crazing before use.

Material numbers: Elegoo publishes no reachable TDS. Use tensile 32 MPa ±10 %, flexural 35-45 MPa, elongation about 44 %, Shore D 78-81, HDT unknown (assume ≤55 °C). For cyclic gear teeth and sustained loads, design to about 6 MPa rather than 8.5 MPa, because no fatigue or creep data exists for tough photopolymers.

To turn the shop data into verified=true, the session network must allow the shop hosts (eu.store.bambulab.com, tymoty.com, loziska-policka.cz, 3djake.com, elegoo.com, files.seeedstudio.com). Only waveshare.com hosts are allowed now.
research.summary:
Research A (printed mechanics, servo coupling, common bearings), 26 Nov 2026.

**Servo output (verified on Waveshare's page, drawing and STEP files):**
- SC09 / SCS0009 output is a 20T spline, OD 3.95, root Ø3.45, about 2.2 mm toothed plus a 0.29 mm chamfer, with a 0.8 mm plain Ø4.0 collar below the teeth.
- Centre hole is Ø1.6 x 5.0 deep, so M2 is likely, but the thread is not modelled.
- The servo has metal gears and a plain (sliding) output bearing.
- Supplied plastic horns: hub Ø6.9-7.4, height 3.7-4.1. The Seeed datasheet lists 3 horns and 3 screws in the box; Waveshare's package list says only "SC09 Servo x1".
- Hobbyists couple printed parts by gluing the original horn into a printed recess, not by printing the spline.

**Elegoo Tough (no official TDS reachable):**
- Amazon listings give tensile 32.1 MPa ±10 %, flexural 35-45 MPa, elongation about 44 %, Shore D 78-81. No HDT, fatigue or creep data was found.
- Field reports on printed resin gears are mixed: a resin gearbox powdered and broke while PLA held, but a filled resin survived. No m0.5 data exists.

**Gear strength (my own Lewis calculation, verified=false):**
- In this space the printed bevel pair reaches the 8.5 MPa allowable at only about 0.013-0.017 N.m at the arm, and breaks at about 0.05-0.065 N.m.
- So the clutch must slip at about 0.010 N.m and homing must stay below that, instead of 0.06 / 0.043 N.m. The arm needs 0.004 N.m, so this is feasible.

**Bearings:**
- MR63ZZ, MR74ZZ and 6700ZZ (the design's bearings) are all sold by the Bambu Lab EU store, a common 3D-printing source (6-packs and 2-packs).
- They are also standard RC sizes and are listed by SK/CZ bearing shops (tymoty.com, loziska-policka.cz).
- 623/624/625/688/608/6701 ZZ and MR105 are common at 3D-printing and RC shops.
- MR83/85/93/115/128, 683, 684 and 6800/61800 are specialist-only.

**Caveat:** only waveshare.com hosts were reachable. All prices and stock figures come from search snippets (verified=false), and the shop hosts must be allowed to verify them.

Files:
- Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/prieskum_tlacene/dokazy.json
- Gear calc: /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/prieskum_tlacene/gear_lewis.py and /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/prieskum_tlacene/gear_lewis.json
- Downloaded servo/horn STEP files and drawing: /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/prieskum_tlacene/dl/

Research B: which hardware-store and fastener-shop parts a hobbyist in Slovakia can actually buy, checked against the no-metal-work rule. Limits on the evidence: WebFetch could not reach www.hornbach.sk, www.tymoty.com or www.laskarduino.sk (they are outside the session's allowed network), so following the tool's instruction I stopped trying more shop sites. Everything below comes from WebSearch result summaries, not from opened pages, so verified=false throughout. Hornbach.sk, OBI.sk, Bauhaus.sk and Merkury are not indexed by the search engine. Hornbach CZ is used as a stand-in, assuming (unverified) that its range matches Hornbach SK. Main results: (1) Common in Hornbach-type stores: M3 DIN 912 8.8 zinc screws at 10/16/20/25/40 mm in 10-packs (about 1.0-1.4 EUR per pack); M4 DIN 912 at 12/30/40/50; M5 from 10 to 100 mm; DIN 7985 M3x10/16/20; M2x10 Phillips screws; A2 nuts and washers; a 200-piece spring box (46 CZK); a 225-piece O-ring box (169 CZK); single A2 compression springs; Loctite 243 (5 ml, 249 CZK); UHU plus endfest epoxy. M3 ISO 7380 / DIN 7991 in A2, DIN 913 M3 set screws and all M2/M2.5 sizes come from CZ fastener or 3D-printing shops (Tymoty, 3DJake, Prusa, Rotorama, LaskaKit), not from big-box stores. (2) Long M3 screws: 30 and 40 mm are common; 35/45/50 mm were found only at RS / Accu / McMaster level. ISO 4762 gives b=18 mm for M3, M3 screws up to 20 mm are fully threaded, and the standard M3 range ends at about 30 mm. Whether a longer screw has a plain shank is up to the maker: Hornbach DE M3x10-25 are full thread, Hornbach AT M4x40 is partial thread, and the stainless M3 found was full thread. Shank diameter is about 2.86-3.00 mm for M3 and 3.82-4.00 mm for M4 (from a garbled table). In a 3 or 4 mm bearing bore that leaves 0 to 0.14 / 0.18 mm of diametral play, which Loctite 638 can fill (gaps up to 0.25 mm), but a shank is not guaranteed. (3) Threaded rod M3/M4 is sold only in 1 m lengths (Hornbach CZ M3 A2: 39 CZK), so it needs cutting and is excluded. (4) Nuts and washers: DIN 934 M3 A2 and DIN 125 M3 A2 are common; DIN 985 M3 is at HOBBY-MAX.CZ; DIN 9021 3.2 comes in brass singles; DIN 433 and DIN 439 M3 were not found in SK/CZ retail; polyamide DIN 125 washers are at Hornbach CZ (4.3 mm) and TME (M3/M4, minimum order 100); small PTFE washers were NOT found in retail. (5) Springs: assortment boxes do not state wire diameter. Single springs are available from Hornbach CZ (A2 6.6x33x0.7, 9.2x66x0.8 and others) and from Exvalos (CZ, CSN 02 6020 standard springs, 1x9x24x8.5 and 1x9x30x10.5 at 0.71 EUR). Rough calculation: in a Ø9 space a commonly sold spring gives about 26 N usable at most, while the current clutch (μ 0.12, r_m 3.6 mm, 2 faces) needs 69 N. A common-parts clutch needs μ·r_m·faces of at least about 2.3e-3 m. (6) The standard 225-piece O-ring box has, inferred from its listed sizes, only cross-sections of 1 or 2 mm at inner diameters 3-6 mm and none at 1.5 mm; single 1.5 mm O-rings are sold by Tymoty (Dichtomatik). (7) Brass inserts: CNC Kitchen M3x5.7 (OD 4.6, hole 4.0) at Prusa and 3DJake, ruthex M3/M2.5/M2 at 3DJake, and a LaskaKit set (M2 OD 3.5). Heat-setting does not work in thermoset resin, so inserts must be glued in. (8) Magnets: 4x2 and 5x2 mm in packs from umagnets.com/sk, Alza.cz (Ø4 x 50 pieces, 106 CZK, thickness not stated), filamentia (4x2, 0.17 EUR) and yourmagnets (3x2 N52, 0.17 EUR). One 3x2 listing is magnetized across the diameter, so check the magnetization direction before buying. (9) Glues: Loctite 243 is in Hornbach CZ, but its data sheet advises against use on plastics (stress cracking). Loctite 638 10 ml with activator is 19.00 EUR at umakov.sk, with stock at Slovak branches. Loctite 641 and Slovak-store epoxy listings were not found. Notes and the calculation script are in /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/prieskum_zelezarstvo/ (notes.md, calc_springs.py).

Required axial preload for 0.06 N·m with 2 friction faces: μ 0.12 / r_m 3.6 mm gives 69 N (the current DIN 2093 design); μ 0.2 / r_m 5 gives 30 N; μ 0.3 / r_m 5 gives 20 N; μ 0.2 / r_m 6.5 gives 23 N. The data sheet advises against use on plastics (stress cracking). Use it only metal-to-metal (screw into nut), never a screw into resin.
Gaps up to 0.25 mm; stocked at Slovak branches of an industrial tool chain. Loctite 641 not found in retail.
Slovak store listing not indexed; the product type is standard hardware-store stock.

recommendations: Design around the screws a big-box store reliably carries: M3 DIN 912 at 10/16/20/25/40 mm, M4 DIN 912 at 12/30/40 mm, M5 at 10-100 mm, M3 DIN 7985 at 10/16/20 mm. Avoid M3x35/45/50; they were found only at RS / Accu / McMaster-level suppliers. For A2 ISO 7380 M3 (10/16/30) or DIN 913 M3, name Tymoty (CZ, EUR prices) or Fabory SK as the source.
Reinforcing rods: make printed holes blind and exactly long enough for a stock M3x40 (or M3x25 / M3x30) bonded with 2K epoxy, so nothing is cut. Do not use threaded rod (sold only per metre).

Do not design on the assumption that a screw has a precision plain shank. M3 up to 20 mm is fully threaded, M3x35-50 is outside the ISO range, and Hornbach DE M3 up to 25 mm is full thread. If a 3 or 4 mm journal on a screw shank is used (MR63 / MR74), require a caliper check (shank about 2.86-3.00 / 3.82-4.00 mm, about 0-0.14 / 0-0.18 mm play) and bond with Loctite 638 + activator. Better: let bearings sit on large printed rings (like the 6700 on the Ø13 ring) and use the screw only as a bonded core.

Clutch: the DIN 2093 disc spring and its 69 N preload are not compatible with common parts. The most force found in a Ø9 space from a buyable spring is about 26 N (CSN 02 6020 1x9x24x8.5 from Exvalos, or a box spring that must be measured). Redesign so μ·r_m·faces is at least about 2.3e-3 m, e.g. r_m 5-6.5 mm with μ 0.2-0.3 on printed resin or PA washer faces. Set the preload by geometry (a screw that bottoms on a printed stop compresses the spring to a fixed length), not by tightening torque; the user has no torque screwdriver.
O-rings: the 225-piece box offers cross-sections of 1 and 2 mm (no 1.5) at small inner diameters (3-6 mm), so size grooves for CS 1.0 or 2.0, or buy single Dichtomatik NBR 1.5 mm O-rings from Tymoty.

Threaded inserts: specify glue-in (epoxy) installation, because resin is a thermoset. CNC Kitchen / ruthex M3x5.7 have OD 4.6 and a nominal 4.0 hole; size the printed pocket for the glue and confirm with a test print. For M2, plan on LaskaKit OD 3.5 or ruthex M2x4, or use M3 nuts in printed hex pockets instead.

Glue choice: never put Loctite 243 on screws that go into resin (the data sheet warns of stress cracking). Use 2K epoxy for metal-to-resin joints, and Loctite 638 (+ activator) only for metal-to-metal bearing seats.
Thrust and anti-friction washers: small PTFE washers are not commonly available. Use polyamide DIN 125 washers (Hornbach 4.3 mm, TME M3/M4) or printed resin washers with grease.
Magnets: specify axially magnetized 4x2 or 5x2 discs (umagnets.com/sk, Alza, filamentia). The cheap 3x2 umagnets listing is magnetized across the diameter.

Before the final bill of materials, have hornbach.sk, tymoty.com, laskarduino.sk (and gme.sk, obi.sk, bauhaus.sk) allowed in the session's network settings so prices and stock can be confirmed on the actual pages. Everything here is from search summaries and is unverified.

r.name_sk: Ruka B1 – tlačené kužeľové kolieska, skrutka M4 ako hriadeľ, magnetická trecia spojka
r.summary_sk: Pohon ruky B1 zachováva kinematiku v2: stojace servo SCS0009 v stĺpe, jeden kužeľový pár, čiernu zátku a ruku na ložisku 6700. Vzhľad sa nemení: zapustená zátka, krúžok Ø13, medzera 3,7 mm, aspoň 1,0 mm v celom rozsahu. Kolieska (12/18 zubov, modul 0,667, záber 25°), hriadeľ pastorka, spojka na páke serva, unášač a náboj sú tlačené z Elegoo Tough. Hriadeľ ruky je bežná skrutka DIN 912 M4×20 s nalepeným kolieskom a ložiskami MR74. Trecia spojka nemá pružinu: drží ju 4–7 magnetov 5×2 mm proti podložke DIN 125 M10, nastavuje sa mincami na 0,0136–0,016 N·m a zuby pri tom majú najviac 7,7 MPa (dovolené 8,5). Nič sa nereže, nevŕta ani nesústruží, okrem orezania plastovej páčky serva. Neoverené ostáva: životnosť tlačených zubov, presná sila magnetov, skutočná hodnota 3 % momentu serva a pevnosť hornej časti stĺpa pri záťaži L5. Tú treba overiť výpočtom MKP aj so zapojením bočného krytu; slabina tam bola už vo v2.
changes_vs_v2: Bevel pair: the brass 16/24 m0.5 pair (pinion hub had to be turned off) becomes a PRINTED 12/18 pair, m 0.6667, PA 25 deg, ha* 0.9, hf* 1.15, rack tip radius 0.38m, b 2.8. Pitch radii (4/6), apex O (39,3,-17) and ratio 1.5 are kept, so the v2 envelopes and clearances stay valid (pinion crown r 4.50 vs 4.42, gear crown r 6.33 vs 6.28).

Vertical shaft: steel D3 h6 with a D-flat becomes a PRINTED shaft with three sections: hex 4 AF (coupler), D3 journal (MR63), D2.5 D-key (pinion). The pinion slips on the key and sits on a printed 0.42 shim on the MR63 inner race; no glue, so it can be replaced.
Servo coupler: brass sleeve + M2 grub screw becomes a PRINTED cup (r 4.5). The supplied plastic horn is trimmed (arm cut off, two flats filed) and epoxied in; the shaft hex press-fits by hand.

Arm shaft: turned steel D4 with D4/D3 step, tapped M2 end and e-clip becomes a stock DIN 912 M4x20 (8.8, fully threaded). The printed 18T gear is epoxied on its inner end; the MR74 inner races are bonded on the thread with Loctite 638 + activator.

Clutch: D-flat washer + brass flange + DIN 2093 disc spring (69 N) + M2 screw, slip 0.06 N.m, becomes a MAGNETIC friction clutch. A printed drive hub on the M4 head has 8 pockets for 5x2 mm axially magnetised discs behind a 0.25 mm skin, pulled against a DIN 125 M10 washer bonded in the arm hub. Slip 0.0136-0.016 N.m, set by magnet count and checked with coins; no spring, no creep, internal force loop (no bearing preload).

Arm retention/removal: the clutch-stack screw is replaced by the drive hub press-fitted on the knurled M4 head (printed hex 3 AF key in the socket) and captured in the arm hub by a bonded printed lip. The arm pulls off with a firm pull (breakaway) and pushes back on.
6700 moved 2 mm outboard (x 55.5..59.5): outer race epoxied in the arm hub, inner race slides on the plug seat. Seat D10 lengthened to x 59.5, seat bore D5.0.
Homing stop: the D1 steel pin on the ring end becomes a printed lug on the seat (6 o'clock, x 52.5..55.0, r 5.0..6.6) plus a rib in the arm hub. Contact at -51 deg, 0.58 mm at -45.

Plug (zatka) internals: cavity r 6.9 (was 6.8); plug and boss 6 o'clock slots widened to |y-3| <= 5.3 (was 5.0); D7 bore with printed spacer, A2 moved into the seat (x 52.60..55.10) so its steel race stiffens the D13/D10 step; A1 at x 44.54..47.04. The D2 h6 dowels become two printed D2.4 pegs. Outside of the plug unchanged.

Column: 2x D3 silver-steel rods per side (cut to 46/31 mm) become 1x DIN 912 M3x40 per side, epoxied off-centre at (39.0, 12.35) in the back leg, head in a counterbore in the foot. The front leg cannot take a screw because of the cable slot.
Servo settings: homing torque limit 15 % becomes 3 % (0.010 N.m at the arm, below the clutch); running limit 15 %; fallback slip-homing at 10 %.
PORON 0.5 (specialist foam) on the servo pocket is replaced by common self-adhesive felt/foam tape, or omitted (anti-rattle only).
r.final_design:
LEFT side, frame B (mm). The RIGHT side is the mirror x -> -x; every check was run for both sides.

1 SERVO + COLUMN (unchanged from v2 except the reinforcement)
- SCS0009 earless, standing, output up on (39, 3). Case x 32.95..45.05, y -14.3..8.9, z -66.5..-45. Same pocket column in T_spodok as v2.
- Reinforcement: one DIN 912 M3x40 per side.
  * Epoxied in a D3.3 blind hole at (39.0, 12.35), thread z -75..-35.
  * Head in a D6x3 counterbore in the foot (z -78..-75).
  * The front leg cannot take one: the cable slot is below and the strut is only 4.0 wide above.
- Servo held by the coupler on the shaft plus the printed snap tab. Thin felt/foam tape instead of PORON (optional).

2 VERTICAL DRIVE
- Coupler (printed cup, r 4.5, z -43.5..-35.5).
  * Pocket for the supplied single-arm horn: arm cut off with side cutters, two flats filed to AF 6.2, 2K epoxy.
  * A shoulder above the horn hub, so pressing the coupler pushes on the horn, not through the bond.
  * Hex socket 4 AF on top. The horn screw is driven through the socket first.
- Vertical shaft (printed, axis vertical):
  * hex 4 AF at z -39.6..-36.1, hand press fit in the coupler, no backlash;
  * D3 journal through the D4 tongue hole and the bore of B1 = MR63ZZ (bonded in the tongue, z -26.35..-23.85, unchanged);
  * D2.5 D-key from z -23.43 to -20.47.
- Pinion 12T (printed):
  * envelope: toe z -20.47 (r 2.75), crown r 4.50 at z -22.67, heel root z -23.43;
  * slips on the D-key and sits on a printed 0.42 shim (r 1.55..1.9) on the MR63 inner race;
  * back face relieved 0.2 over r 1.95..3.6;
  * held down by the mesh thrust; the gear above stops it lifting.
- Backlash is set only with the pinion shim (printed 0.30 / 0.42 / 0.50 / 0.60).
- Service lift 4.5 (plug out): the shaft top reaches -15.97 (slot roof -15.5); the lifted hex (-35.1) clears the coupler top (-35.5).

3 GEAR PAIR
- Straight bevel, Sigma 90, apex O (39, 3, -17), ratio 1.5 (servo 300 deg -> arm 200 deg; -51..+135 uses 279 deg of the servo).
- m 0.6667 (heel), PA 25 deg, ha* 0.9, hf* 1.15, rack tip radius 0.38m, x 0, b 2.8, R 7.211, delta 33.69 / 56.31 deg.
- Tooth form generated by rolling the rack: Lewis Y 0.398 / 0.498, Kf 1.40 / 1.52, contact ratio 1.29, no interference, top land 0.25 at the pinion toe.
- Gear 18T envelope: toe x 41.14 r 3.87; crown x 42.50 r 6.33; root x 43.64; back x 44.24 (relieved to x 44.04 for r > 3).
- Printing: axis vertical, 20 um layers, supports on the back faces only; thin each flank by 0.02 for backlash; PTFE grease or graphite (test on scrap first).

4 PLUG CARTRIDGE (zatka, black, printed on its axis)
- Outside identical to v2:
  * neck r 11 (x 38.6..40.6), body r 13.5, face recessed 1.0 below the approved surface, ring D13 to x 52.5;
  * 3x M2x10 countersunk at r 9.0 (12/4/8 o'clock) into glued M2 brass inserts in the boss;
  * 2 printed D2.4 pegs replace the dowels (holes at r 9.0, 10 and 2 o'clock).
- Inside:
  * gear cavity r 6.9 to x 44.54;
  * plug and boss 6 o'clock slots |y-3| <= 5.3;
  * D7 bore from the cavity to an outboard shoulder at x 55.10, holding A2 = MR74 (x 52.60..55.10), a printed spacer sleeve and A1 = MR74 (x 44.54..47.04), slipped in from the cavity side;
  * D10 seat x 52.5..59.5 with bore D5.0, and the homing lug at 6 o'clock (x 52.5..55.0, r 5.0..6.6, 4.5 wide).
- Arm shaft = DIN 912 M4x20 (major dia >= 3.93 selected by calipers):
  * head bearing face x 60.0 (0.5 off the seat end), tip x 40.0 (1.6 from the boss face);
  * printed 18T gear epoxied on the thread (bore D4.1), with a printed 0.30 shim on the A1 inner race; mounting distance fixed by this shim;
  * A1/A2 inner races bonded on the thread with Loctite 638 + activator.
- Thrust paths:
  * outward gear thrust: A1 outer race -> spacer -> A2 outer race -> shoulder;
  * the shaft never sees an inward force (inward pushes on the arm go through the arm hub into the ring end face);
  * the mesh limits inward float to the backlash.
- Bench assembly:
  1. A2, spacer and A1 into the bore.
  2. Gear and shim held in the cavity.
  3. Push the M4 in from outboard (638 on the bearing zones, epoxy in the gear bore); hold the gear on the shim while it cures.

5 ARM SIDE (inside the arm, dx -1.0)
- 6700ZZ: outer race epoxied in the printed arm hub (bore D15, x 55.5..59.5); inner race slides on the D10 seat (slip, stationary gravity load).
- Arm-hub flange x 59.5/60.0..60.6 (inner r 5.0) with a DIN 125 M10 washer (10.5x20x2) bonded flat on its outboard face (x 60.6..62.6, friction partner).
- Drive hub (printed), captive in the arm hub behind a bonded printed lip ring (x 66.4..67.6, inner r 10.4):
  * pocket over the whole M4 head (x 60.0..64.0, diametral press 0.03-0.08 on the knurl);
  * printed hex 3 AF key in the head socket;
  * boss r 4.5 (0.75 to the washer hole);
  * disc r 11.0, x 62.6..65.9; friction face = 0.25 skin at x 62.6, printed face down;
  * 8 blind pockets at r 7.7 for 5x2 axial discs (N38; N52 if needed), alternating polarity, open outboard and reachable through the lip opening.
- Clutch:
  * preload = magnet pull on the washer, an internal loop, so no bearing load and no spring;
  * faces dry and degreased (mu 0.25-0.4); typically 4-7 magnets;
  * calibration: arm forward-horizontal, servo holding, coins at 60 mm from the shoulder axis. 2 EUR + 50 c (16.3 g, 0.0136 N.m including about 0.004 from the arm) must HOLD; 2 EUR + 50 c + 10 c (20.4 g, 0.0160) must SLIP. Add or remove magnets until both pass.
- Arm removal: arm cover off, firm pull; the drive hub leaves the M4 head with the arm.
- Arm re-fit: push on and rotate slightly until the hex key drops into the socket (the clutch lets the drive hub turn).
- Homing stop: rib in the arm hub (x 53.0..55.0, r 5.5..8.5) hits the seat lug at arm -51 deg. The arm slides on at rest pose without the rib meeting the lug.

6 FIRMWARE
- Running torque limit 15 % (0.034 N.m servo, 0.051 arm). It is above the clutch, so the clutch alone caps the tooth load.
- 65 C limit; range -45..+135; limit acceleration so the dynamic torque stays <= 0.004 N.m.
- Homing at power-up and after any unexpected load peak:
  * torque limit 3 % (0.0068 N.m servo, 0.010 N.m arm), slow, towards -51 deg; detect the stall; store the offset;
  * order: arm need 0.004-0.008 < homing 0.010 < clutch 0.0136-0.016 < pinion root limit 0.0176 (Lewis x Kf at 8.5 MPa) / 0.0246 (Lewis);
  * fallback if 3 % does not move the arm reliably: slip homing at 10 %. The teeth still see at most the clutch torque, because the clutch is downstream of the pair.

7 TORSO ASSEMBLY (as v2)
1. Shaft up through the MR63 from below.
2. Pinion + shim on top.
3. Lift the shaft 4.5.
4. Slide the servo in with the coupler.
5. Lower the hex into the coupler.
6. Fit the cap (v2 notch passes the shaft).
7. Insert the plug cartridge: pegs, 3x M2.
8. Check backlash by rocking the M4 head; change the pinion shim if needed (plug out).
9. Push the arm on, then the arm cover.

8 SERVO SWAP (about 10 min, as v2)
1. Arm cover off, pull the arm off.
2. 3 screws, plug out.
3. Cap off.
4. Lift the shaft.
5. Servo out along +X.

9 RIGHT SIDE
- Mirror x -> -x.
- The web is the J1 cradle end wall, as in v2.
- Servo to J1 cradle 0.56; coupler and pinion to the sweep 1.60 / 1.61.

r.noise:
* **Teeth.** Only one gear mesh is added: a greased resin-on-resin straight bevel pair.
  * It turns at most about 0.25 rev/s at the pinion, so the mesh frequency is about 3 Hz and no tonal whine is produced.
  * Polymer teeth damp impacts better than the brass pair of v2.
  * The servo's own metal gear train and motor remain the dominant sources.
* **Backlash.** Taken up at rest silently: the arm hangs at 0 deg, where the gravity torque passes through zero, so there is no knock under load.
* **Clutch.** No noise in normal running. A slip is a soft scrape, with no snapping, because the steel washer is uniform and gives no magnetic detents.
* **Other parts.** No rattling parts: the pinion is held by its own thrust and the drive hub is pressed on.
* **Homing.** At 3 % torque the arm reaches the stop with a faint tick.
* Noise was not measured; all of the above is a qualitative estimate.
r.durability:
* **Teeth.**
  * No sustained tooth load: the arm rests at 0 deg with about zero gravity torque.
  * Running root stress <= 3.9 MPa (Lewis x Kf) and Hertz about 14 MPa.
  * At the clutch-slip level (rare events) <= 7.7 MPa (pinion) / 6.7 MPa (gear).
  * Archard estimate, k = 1e-5 mm3/N.m (no data for Elegoo Tough, uncertain by about 10x): about 0.01 mm flank wear per 10^7 engagements, i.e. about 0.3 deg extra arm backlash; with 10x the wear rate about 1.5 deg.
  * Field reports of printed resin gearboxes powdering exist, but they ran at far higher loads; still unverified.
  * The 12T pinion wears first. Replacement: plug out (3 screws), lift the pinion off the D-key, drop a new one on with its shim; about 15 min plus about 30 min printing.
  * The 18T gear is replaced as a unit with a new M4x20; the MR74s can be reused if the 638 is released by heating the screw, or replaced (EUR 1-3 each). The plug stays.
* **Creep.** No resin part carries a permanent preload:
  * the clutch force is magnetic and closes between the drive hub and the washer;
  * the gear thrust only exists under load;
  * the plug screws are snug;
  * the column screw carries load only under L5.
  * The drive-hub press fit on the M4 head relaxes (estimate 45-120 N fresh, 13-60 N long term). This only lowers the breakaway force of the arm. If it gets too easy, reprint the drive hub 0.03 tighter.
* **Clutch.** Face pressure 0.05 MPa and about 4 mm of sliding per slip, so wear is negligible. Skin wear raises the magnet force slightly, so the slip torque cannot fall over life. A drift of the friction coefficient is possible, so recheck with the coin test about once a year and change the magnet count if needed.
* **Bearings.** All rotating joints are ball bearings and no printed bushing slides in normal running. The vertical shaft does not turn in the MR63 bore (the pinion thrust drives the inner race). The 6700 inner race only slides axially on the seat.
* **Homing stop.** The rib in the arm hub is the sacrificial part. Homing loads give 1.4 MPa; a push of 3 N at the arm tip gives 16 MPa, which is acceptable short-term. A 10 N push would dent it (54 MPa). The arm hub is a cheap reprint. A Hall-sensor upgrade removes the stop entirely.
* **Print or fit drift.** Test coupons are needed for the D3 journal in the MR63, the D7 bore, the D10 seat and the drive-hub press fit before printing the final parts.
r.strength:
All hand calculations are in strength_b1.py (strength_b1.log). Allowable 8.5 MPa long term; 6 MPa is used as the target for cyclic tooth loads.

GEARS (gears.py / gear_chosen.json; Lewis on the numerically generated tooth, mean bevel section)
- Pinion root, Lewis / Lewis x Kf:
  * arm need 0.004 N.m: 1.38 / 1.93 MPa;
  * running 0.008: 2.76 / 3.87;
  * clutch 0.0136: 4.70 / 6.57;
  * clutch 0.0160: 5.52 / 7.73;
  * 0.0165 (coin-test upper bound + arm-weight uncertainty): 5.70 / 7.98. All <= 8.5.
- Gear root (Lewis x Kf) <= 6.94 MPa.
- Arm torque at 8.5 MPa: 0.0246 (Lewis) / 0.0176 (Lewis x Kf), against 0.0142 / 0.0100 for the v2 pair printed in resin.
- Hertz at the pitch point: 14.4 MPa (running), 20.4 MPa (slip), E 2 GPa assumed.

VERTICAL DRIVE (at 0.0165 at the arm, i.e. 0.011 at the pinion)
- Pinion D-key bearing 2.7 MPa.
- Shaft D2.5 torsion 4.9 MPa; shaft D3 torsion 2.3 MPa; bending at the MR63 4.6 MPa.
- Coupler hex 0.45 MPa; horn flats 0.39 MPa. The epoxy-to-PA bond carries almost nothing, because the flats carry the torque.

ARM SHAFT (M4x20, minor diameter 3.14)
- Torsion 3 MPa.
- Bending under the largest tilting couple the magnet-held friction face can pass when the arm is pushed sideways (9 N x 10.5 mm, plus mesh): 36 MPa in steel. A printed D4 tube would see 18.7 MPa, which is why the arm shaft is a screw.
- Gear epoxy bond 0.23 MPa. Loctite 638 bond on the MR74 races 0.37 MPa.
- Drive-hub hex key 1.2 MPa; drive-hub pocket edge pressure under the tilt couple 5.1 MPa.

ARM RETENTION
- Magnets 6-9 N plus the press fit (about 13-60 N long term).
- Lifting the robot by an arm (about 11 N): holds.
- A 30 N yank: the arm pops off without damage (breakaway, by design).

CLUTCH (magnets.py: charge model calibrated to catalogue pull)
- 5x2 N38 through the 0.25 skin on a 2 mm washer: 0.93-1.32 N per magnet.
- At mu 0.25: 6 magnets give 0.013 N.m, 8 give 0.017.
- Dry faces mu 0.25-0.4 cover the window with 4-7 magnets. Face pressure 0.05 MPa.

HOMING STOP (contact 1.1 x 2.0 mm at r 6.05)
- Homing at the clutch-slip level: 1.4 MPa.
- 3 N at the arm tip: 16 MPa (short term); 10 N: 54 MPa, which dents it.
- Lug root shear at 3 N: 3.2 MPa.

PLUG (L5 couple 0.72 N.m)
- Seat D10/D5.0 between A2 and the 6700: 7.8 MPa (about 9.4 with Kt 1.2). Same section as v2.
- Ring D13/D7 root 4.7 MPa (Kt 1.3).
- Plug screws and inserts as v2 (about 53 N each).

COLUMN (column_b1.py, transformed section, L5, Kt 1.3)
- C-channel: 2.6-2.8 MPa.
- z -48: 8.54 MPa with the M3x40 at x 39.0 (allowable 8.5; v2 rods 3.92).
- z -44..-36: 6.1-6.5 MPa.
- Screw force <= 155 N, giving a mean bond shear of 1.3 MPa.
- z -33..-30, where the back leg narrows to x 34.4..38.4 plus the 4.0 mm strut: 22-23 MPa with or without reinforcement.

risks: Printed tooth life and backlash growth are unproven. There is no wear or fatigue data for m0.5-0.8 MSLA gears in Elegoo Tough, and field reports of resin gearboxes are mixed. Mitigation: low stresses (running <= 3.9 MPa with Kf), lubrication, a cheap and easy pinion swap, and an endurance test of a printed pair (1e4-1e5 cycles at the clutch torque) before committing.

The clutch slip torque depends on the friction coefficient (0.15-0.4) and the real magnet force (+-40 %). The coin calibration and the 8-pocket count adjustment cover this, but drift over time (transfer film, dust, humidity) means a yearly recheck. Any grease on the clutch faces drops it below the useful window.
The homing stop is medium-duty. A push above about 3-5 N at the arm tip past -51 deg dents the printed rib (sacrificial part in the arm hub). The Hall-sensor upgrade removes the stop altogether.

The arm is held by magnets plus a press fit that relaxes (estimated 13-60 N long term). A yank pops the arm off, which is harmless but may surprise the user. If it is too loose, reprint the drive hub tighter.

Upper column (z -33..-30) at 22-23 MPa under L5 with the real section. Inherited from v2 (the judge's calc used the full leg width) and not fixable with screws. FE with the side-cap load share is needed, or a thicker upper column (about 9 MPa with a solid wall x 34.4..38.4 from y -16 to 15.5 around the shaft), before printing T_spodok. The z -48 section sits at 8.54 against 8.5.
Plug seat D10 under L5: 7.8 MPa nominal, about 9.4 with Kt. Same as v2 and above the long-term allowable, but L5 is a rare abuse case. FE pending.

The M4 thread used as the bearing seat (Loctite 638) can sit up to 0.035-0.09 off-centre in the 4.000 bore. Mitigation: pick screws with major diameter >= 3.93 by calipers. A tight mesh spot would show as a jerk; it is corrected with the pinion shim or another screw.
The 3 % homing torque may be below what the SCS0009 can deliver against its own gearbox friction. Fallback: slip homing at 10 % (teeth still capped by the clutch).

Printed fits (D3 journal in MR63, D7 bore, D10 seat, coupler hex, drive-hub press) depend on the user's printer, resin shrinkage and post-cure. They need test coupons, especially the 0.25 mm skin and the 20 um gear prints.
The 6700ZZ had no confirmed Slovak shop (Bambu EU, Robitronic, Albeco, bike shops). It is the least common bought part.

The cable slot in the front leg is placed on the assumption that the cable leaves the front end of the case (v2 open item). If it leaves at the output end, the slot moves to the back leg, and the M3x40 then has to move.
unverified: All shop availability and prices come from search snippets (research A/B and this session); no shop page was opened. Hornbach CZ M4x20 and Tymoty M2x20 were seen only in search results. The web-search budget ran out before the 5x2 magnet and DIN 125 M10 listings could be re-checked.
Elegoo Tough properties (modulus about 2 GPa assumed; UTS 29-32 MPa from Amazon listings), fatigue, creep, and friction coefficient on steel. Grease compatibility with the resin.
Magnet forces: model calibrated to catalogue pull values. The washer saturation factor (0.6-0.85) and the effect of alternating poles are estimates.

Real tooth geometry, backlash and transmission error were not checked with a 3D tooth model. Only the 2D virtual-gear analysis was done (contact ratio, interference, Lewis). No 3D mesh interference check.
Wear-rate constant (Archard k = 1e-5 mm3/N.m, uncertain by about 10x) and life estimate.
Press-off force of the drive hub on the knurled M4 head, and its relaxation.
Whether the SCS0009 moves the arm reliably at a 3 % torque limit, and its load/stall detection at that level.
Supplied horn type and screw size (the servo box contents vary by seller).
SC09 cable exit end (decides the cable-slot leg and the M3 screw position).
Column and plug FE (L5 upper column 22-23 MPa by hand; side-cap load share not counted).
Arm axial tolerance stack (+-0.1 estimated), so the +135 gap may be 0.9-1.1.
Noise (qualitative only).

r.name_sk: B2 – maximum tlače: vytlačené kužeľové kolieska 12/18, živicové puzdrá bez ložísk a magnetická spojka s jedinou polohou
r.summary_sk: Všetko špeciálne je vytlačené z Elegoo Tough: kužeľové kolieska (12/18 zubov, modul 0,65, uhol záberu 25°), pastorok s hriadeľom a drážkovaním na servo v jednom kuse, koleso s hriadeľom ruky v jednom kuse, puzdrá, vložka jazýčka aj spojka. Kupuje sa len servo, štyri skrutky M2, štyri mosadzné vložky M2, tri magnety Ø4×2, jedna veľká oceľová podložka M8, lepidlo a grafitový prášok. Nie sú tam žiadne ložiská, oceľové hriadele ani tyčinky a nič sa nereže ani nevŕta do kovu. Ruku chráni magnetická spojka s troma zúbkami, ktorá zapadne len v jednej polohe. Keď niekto ruku otočí silou, spojka preskočí, a keď servo prejde cez polohu ruky, sama zase zapadne, takže netreba nulovanie nárazom na doraz. Stĺp v trupe nepotrebuje oceľové tyčinky, stačí ho vyplniť do voľného miesta. Vzhľad ruky a medzera 3,7 mm ostávajú ako vo v2. Neoverené je opotrebenie živice o živicu (životnosť od mesiacov po roky), presná sila spojky (nastaví sa na robote skúškou s mincami) a výpočet MKP stĺpa; to treba overiť na skúšobnom kuse.
changes_vs_v2: Brass bevel pair m0.5 16/24 (catalogue part, pinion hub turned off) -> PRINTED straight bevel pair m 0.65, z 12/18, alpha 25 deg, profile shift +0.25/-0.25, b 2.5, apex O (39,3,-17) and ratio 1.5 kept. Tooth capacity at 8.5 MPa: 20.3 N.mm vs 12.8 for a printed m0.5 16/24.

Steel D3 shaft with a D-flat + MR63 + brass coupler sleeve + M2 grub screw + 0.5 shim + Loctite 638 -> ONE printed pinion-shaft: printed 20T internal spline coupler r3.5 + D4 shaft + collar r2.7 + 12T pinion. Its collar rests on a printed U-insert, which is the axial reference; no screw.
Tongue: closed ring r3.0..4.4 with MR63 -> C open to +X, r3.2..4.6 with a solid back, holding a replaceable printed U-insert (journal D4.1 x 2.8, anti-rotation flat).

Turned D4->D3 steel arm shaft with M2 tapped end + e-clip + 2x MR74 -> ONE printed gear-spindle: gear + D6 journals (x 44.4..47.8 and 57.2..61.0) in a D6.1 bore of the plug ring + hex AF5 end + glued M2 insert.
6700ZZ arm hub bearing -> printed plain journal: arm hub bore D12.56 on the plug ring D12.5, 8.4 long.

Friction clutch (brass hub flange, 3 steel washers incl. a D-flat one, DIN 2093 disc spring, shims) -> MAGNETIC SINGLE-POSITION DETENT CLUTCH. A printed disc with 3 V-teeth at irregular angles 0/100/220 deg plus a bonded DIN 9021 M8 steel washer; 3 magnets D4x2 in the hub preload it. Slip window 9.3-13.4 N.mm, tuned by a coin test.

Stall homing at 15 % against a hidden stop -> no stall homing: the clutch can only engage in one position, so a slow sync sweep at normal settings re-synchronises (normal motion does it too). EEPROM torque limit 8 % only as a back-up if the clutch jams.
Clutch slip torque 0.06 -> ~0.012 N.m nominal (window 0.0093-0.0134 at the arm), because the printed teeth must stay <= 8.5 MPa even with dry plain-journal friction.
2x D2 h6 dowels on the plug -> 2 printed pins D2.4.

2x D3 silver-steel rods per side cut to 46/31 mm -> none. The column legs are filled into the free space (inboard to the sweep cylinder r~34.65): hand sigma <= 5.1 L / 7.15 R MPa without steel. Fallback: one standard DIN 912 M3x40 bonded from below.
PORON strips -> rigid printed floor pad + printed crush ribs (0.2 interference) + snap tab; the servo rests on the pad, its top limited to 0.5 lift by the strut and a back ledge.

Boss: pinion slot widened to |y-3| <= 5.1, plus a shaft slot |y-3| <= 2.5, x >= 36.5, z -30.0..-24.55, open to +X (also through the stop ring at 6 o'clock) for the lateral insertion of the one-piece pinion-shaft.
Plug: ring D13 -> D12.5 journal from x 52.4 to 61.0, bore D6.1; new keeper finger (closes the U-insert, 0.51 to the shaft); new hold-down post 0.50 above the pinion toe.
Back leg widened toward -Y to y 7.5 above the servo top (z -44.5..-26); it doubles as the back counter-hold when the coupler is pulled off for service.
Servo assembly order changed: servo first, then the pinion-shaft slid in 4.2 mm high along -X and pressed onto the spline, then the U-insert, cap, plug, arm, disc.
r.final_design:
LEFT side, frame B (mm, Z up, front -Y, left +X); RIGHT = mirror x -> -x, checked separately.

SERVO
- Feetech SCS0009, ears cut flush (plastic). Output on the vertical axis (39.0, 3.0); case x 32.95..45.05, y -14.3..8.9, top face z -45.0 (21.5 mm case).
- It rests on a rigid printed floor pad (top z -66.5 for a 21.5 case; lower it for a 25.25 case after measuring). Sideways it is held by printed crush ribs (0.2 interference) on the leg faces and the web, plus the v2 snap tab. Upward travel is limited to 0.5 by the strut (front) and a ledge of the back-leg extension at y 7.5..9.2, z -44.5 (back).
- Cable as v2.
- Settings: EEPROM max torque 8 % (about 18 N.mm), 65 deg C, arm range -45..+135 (+130 if the push-play in 'arm play' must never bring the gap below 1.0).

PINION-SHAFT (printed, one piece, axis (39,3))
- Coupler r 3.5, z -43.5..-40.0, with a printed 20T internal spline. Servo spline OD 3.95 / root 3.45, 2.2 toothed; fit chosen from a coupon with radial offsets 0/+0.02/+0.04/+0.06; the ceiling stays >= 0.5 above the spline tip.
- Shaft D4.0, z -40.0..-24.05.
- Collar r 2.7, z -24.05..-23.21. Its underside rests on the U-insert top and is the axial reference: separating force + weight push it down.
- Pinion 12T.
- Engagement on the spline is nominally 2.0 of 2.2 mm and absorbs the servo/floor tolerance stack.
- Retention: spline friction + a hold-down post on the plug 0.50 above the pinion toe.
- Fallback for the spline: a supplied plastic horn trimmed to a 3.0 mm hub, bonded into a socket (r <= 4.7 above z -40.9).

BEVEL PAIR (printed)
- m 0.65, z 12/18, alpha 25 deg, x +0.25/-0.25, b 2.5, R 7.031, delta 33.69/56.31, contact ratio 1.39, no undercut.
- Ratio 1.5: servo 300 deg gives the arm 200 deg (resolution 0.2 deg).
- Pinion: crown r 4.576 at z -22.40, heel root z -23.21, toe tip z -20.48 (r 2.95).
- Gear: crown r 6.120 at x 42.49, toe x 41.25, heel root x 43.71, back face x 44.21. The back is chamfered 45 deg from r 4.5 to the root (prints without supports); the thrust annulus is r 3.05..4.5.
- Lewis (rack-generated Y, conservative): 8.5 MPa at 20.3 N.mm gear torque.
- Backlash about 0.05 at the gear pitch circle, set by paper/PET shims 0.1 under the gear back (-0.078 each) or a U-insert printed +0.1/+0.2 (-0.052 per 0.1).
- Dry graphite or PTFE dry lubricant.
- Both parts printed axis-vertical, teeth up, no supports on the flanks.

TONGUE + U-INSERT
- Tongue in T_spodok, z -26.85..-24.05: solid block x 34.4..39.0, |y-3| <= 4.6, plus a C-ring r 3.2..4.6 about (39,3) open to +X (|y-3| < 3.2 for x > 39).
- U-insert (printed, replaceable, height variants 0/+0.1/+0.2): r 2.05..3.2, open to +X (opening 4.1), journal D4.1 (0.1 clearance by coupon), flat on the back against rotation.
- The insert slides in along -X around the shaft; the collar holds it down and the plug keeper holds it in +X.

BOSS (T_spodok)
- As v2: solid r <= 12.8, x 34.4..38.4; stop ring r 11.6..12.8, x 38.4..39.1.
- Pinion slot |y-3| <= 5.1 for z >= -24.55, open to +X.
- Shaft slot |y-3| <= 2.5 for x >= 36.5, z -30.0..-24.55, open to +X (cuts the stop ring at 6 o'clock).
- 3 glued M2 brass inserts at r 9.0 (12/4/8 o'clock); 2 holes D2.5 at r 9.0 (10/2 o'clock) for the plug pins.

PLUG (zatka_L, black Tough)
- Neck r 11, x 38.6..40.6; body r 13.5 to the face (approved surface - 1.0); gear cavity r 6.8 to the end wall at x 44.31; 6 o'clock slot |y-3| <= 5.1 for x < 44.0, open to -X.
- 3x M2x10 countersunk screws at r 9.0 into the boss inserts; 2 printed pins D2.4 x 2.
- Ring D13 from the face to x 52.4, then the arm-hub journal D12.5 to x 61.0; through-bore D6.1 from x 44.31 to 61.0.
- Keeper finger x 41.5..44.0, |y-3| <= 1.9, z -26.6..-24.6.
- Hold-down post x 38.6..40.0, y 1.5..4.5, z -19.98..-10.5.
- It clamps the T_bok seat flange against the stop ring as in v2.

GEAR-SPINDLE (printed, one piece)
- Gear + D6.0 spindle. Journal lands x 44.4..47.8 and 57.2..61.0, relief D5.6 between, hex AF5 from x 61.0 to 62.2, glued M2 insert in the end.
- Axial play 0.2 total. Outward, the gear back meets the cavity wall (0.1); the separating force seats it there under load. Inward, the disc meets the ring end (0.1).
- Inserted from the cavity side.

ARM HUB (part of the printed arm body)
- Bore D12.56, x 52.6..61.0 on the D12.5 ring (0.06 clearance by coupon). Counterbore D14 around the D13 ring up to x 52.6, 0.2 from the ring step (inward stop). Flange r 8..14.2 at x 58.5..61.0.
- Outer face at x 61.0: 3 V-grooves at r 12.4..14.0, at 0/100/220 deg.
- 4 magnet pockets D4.1 x 2.9 at r 10.4 (50/160/290/340 deg), normally 3 magnets D4x2 N35, axially magnetised, epoxied, tops 0.9 below the face.

CLUTCH DISC (printed)
- x 61.1..64.5, r 14.2, on the spindle hex, held by an M2x8 screw + Loctite 222, tightened gently.
- A DIN 9021 M8 steel washer (8.4x24x2, zinc-plated) is bonded flush into its inner face.
- 3 V-teeth (flank 30 deg; variants 25/35 deg), height 0.6, engaged 0.3, at r 12.4..14.0, at 0/100/220 deg: they engage at ONE relative angle only.
- Seated magnet-washer gap 1.2.
- T_slip = n F k_sat r tan(beta+phi): 3 magnets nominal 12.3 N.mm, range 8.1-18.1 before tuning.
- Coin test with the arm horizontal and coins taped at the tip (r 72):
  - a 1 EUR coin must hold (9.3 N.mm incl. the arm);
  - 1 EUR + 20 c must slip (13.4 N.mm);
  - tune with the magnet count (2/3/4) and the disc variant (9 steps, 6.9-19.6 N.mm).
- No wind-up below slip. Slipping lowers the magnet force by 33 % (snap-through). Drag while slipping 1.8 N.mm.
- The magnets hold the hub against the disc: axial location without play inside the unit.

SYNC / HOMING
- At power-up the servo sweeps slowly to arm -50 deg, then up to +60, then to the target. The disengaged arm (it hangs, or is held by drag below ~30 deg) is caught exactly when the drive passes it.
- In normal use it re-engages the next time the drive passes the arm's angle.
- The arm<->servo offset (hex step x gear tooth x spline tooth) is calibrated once after assembly.

COLUMN (T_spodok)
- No rods or screws.
- Legs filled into the voxel free space for z -49..-27 in the back band y 7.5..16.5 and the front band y -21..-9, inboard to about the sweep cylinder r 34.65 about Z, with all of these:
  - >= 0.3 to kept static parts (trim 0.1 at the T_paluba edge);
  - >= 1.0 to the sweep;
  - >= 0.5 to the T_stred path;
  - >= 0.3 inboard of the cap removal sweep;
  - outside the drive keep-out (r 4.5 below z -35 / 3.0 above) and the servo slide zone.
- Below the deck: the v2 C-channel.
- Fallback: one DIN 912 M3x40, bonded from below in a printed D3.3 hole (head in a 3.2 counterbore at z -78).

OTHER (unchanged from v2)
- T_bok_L/P notch |y-3| <= 2.5, x 39.0..41.5, z -33.5..-27.5.
- T_paluba trim, F3a_2 at (29.5, 4.0), amplifier and buck moves.
- Arm cover on magnets.

ASSEMBLY
1. Bench:
   - glue the washer into the disc, the magnets into the hub, the M2 inserts into the spindle and the boss;
   - put the gear-spindle into the plug ring.
2. Torso with the cap off: servo in along -X onto the pad.
3. Pinion-shaft held 4.2 high, slid in along -X through the tongue opening and the boss slots, then pressed onto the spline with a printed pusher on the toe face.
4. Lift it 0.5 and slide the U-insert in.
5. Cap on.
6. Plug in along -X (gear engages, keeper and post, pins, 3x M2); shim the backlash.
7. Arm on the ring.
8. Disc on the hex (teeth snap in) + M2x8.
9. Cover.
10. Calibrate the offset; coin test.

SERVICE
- Servo swap ~10 min:
  1. cover, screw, disc, arm off;
  2. plug out, cap off;
  3. insert out (shaft lifted 0.5);
  4. shaft lifted 4.2 (the servo rises 0.5 to the strut/ledge, then the spline releases);
  5. pinion-shaft out along +X, then the servo out along +X.
- Wear parts are small prints: U-insert ~10 min swap, pinion-shaft ~15 min, gear-spindle and disc ~10 min.

RIGHT SIDE
- Mirror x -> -x.
- The web is the J1 cradle end wall (v2); the column fill merges with T_spodok there (0.43 to it).
- All drive clearances re-checked: pinion 1.54, tongue 1.51, boss 1.40 to the sweep; tongue to T_bok_P 0.38.

r.rules_check:
Servo SCS0009/SC09: the only special bought item, already in v2. User operation: cutting the plastic ears and, in the fallback only, trimming a plastic horn (both plastic work, allowed). No metal touched. Source: Waveshare resellers (Botland/TME), AliExpress as backup.

M2x10 countersunk screws (DIN 965 PH / DIN 7991): standard length; Hornbach CZ lists M2x10 countersunk PH in 30-pcs packs, also fastener e-shops. They screw into glued brass inserts. Nothing is cut.

M2x8 DIN 912 / ISO 7380: standard M2 length (Rotorama, 3DJake CNC Kitchen, Tymoty). It only retains the disc; the printed hex carries the torque. Loctite 222 is metal-to-metal into the brass insert.

M2 brass inserts: common 3D-printing item (Prusa, 3DJake ruthex/CNC Kitchen, LaskaKit). Pressed in by hand with 2K epoxy, because heat-setting does not work in resin.

Magnets D4x2 N35, axial: common (umagnets.com/sk, Alza, filamentia), already used in the arm cover. Epoxied into printed pockets; polarity irrelevant (magnet to steel). The user checks the axial magnetisation.

Steel washer DIN 9021 M8 (8.4x24x2, zinc-plated steel): any hardware store. Bonded with epoxy, nothing machined. It must be steel, not A2 (check with a magnet).

2K epoxy, Loctite 222, graphite powder / PTFE dry spray: hardware-store consumables. Loctite 222 is in the user's tool list.

Shims: paper or PET foil cut with the hobby knife.

Optional fallback M3x40 DIN 912: standard length at Hornbach CZ / Tymoty, bonded whole, never cut.

Removed from v2: every bearing (MR63, MR74, 6700), every steel shaft (D3 with D-flat, turned D4->D3 with M2 thread), the brass pinion and gear, the brass coupler sleeve, the grub screw, the brass hub flange, the D-flat washer, the disc spring DIN 2093, the e-clip, the h6 dowels and the cut silver-steel rods.

Rule (c): every special part is printed in Elegoo Tough: gears, pinion-shaft with spline coupler, gear-spindle, bushings (U-insert, plug-ring journals, arm-hub journal), clutch disc and teeth, pins, keeper, post, tools.

Caveat: shop availability comes from the research search snippets (verified=false); the shop hosts were not reachable from this session.
r.noise:
There is one printed bevel pair, running at most 0.75 rev/s at the pinion (arm 180 deg/s, ratio 1.5). With 12 teeth that is a mesh frequency of at most 9 Hz, and the gears are lubricated with graphite or PTFE dry. Resin damps impacts better than brass.

The SCS0009's own metal gear train stays the dominant sound; no extra gear stage is added.

There are no ball bearings to rattle. The plain resin journals are silent when lubricated; dry resin can squeak, so lubricate.

The magnetic detent clutch makes no sound in normal use (no relative motion). It clicks only during a slip (rare: overload or someone forcing the arm).

The sync sweep at power-up is a slow (about 30 deg/s) arm motion.

Not measured; noise is an estimate.
r.durability:
Duty assumed: 3000 arm moves/day of 60 deg. Archard wear with k unknown for Tough on Tough, so 1e-5 / 1e-4 / 1e-3 mm3/(N.m) are carried as a range (calc_b2.json).

Wear depth per year at k 1e-5 / 1e-4 / 1e-3 mm3/(N.m):

| Surface | Pressure | Sliding / year | Depth per year |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-insert (D4.1 x 2.8) | 0.086 MPa | 3.4 km | 0.004 / 0.038 / 0.38 mm |
| Spindle inner land (D6 x 3.4) | 0.047 MPa | 3.4 km | 0.002 / 0.021 / 0.21 mm |
| Collar thrust | 0.042 MPa | 4.1 km | 0.002 / 0.017 / 0.17 mm |
| Arm hub journal (arm weight only) | - | - | < 0.01 mm at any k |

Tooth flank wear is smaller still (Hertz 12 MPa normal).

Resulting backlash growth is 0.006 / 0.057 / 0.57 mm per year, which is 0.06 / 0.56 / 5.6 deg of arm play per year. The U-insert dominates.

Every wear direction loosens the mesh and nothing jams: collar wear lowers the pinion, and journal wear moves the gear and pinion apart.

Creep: no resin spring is preloaded anywhere, because the clutch preload comes only from magnets. The teeth stay <= 8.5 MPa (Lewis) at the highest allowed slip torque, which is the long-term case of an arm pressed against an obstacle.

Expected life: several years if k <= 1e-4 (lubricated), about a year if k ~ 1e-3. Replace parts when the free arm play at hanging exceeds about 2 deg.

Reprinting is easy. All wear parts are small single prints, at most 25 mm tall, all on one plate in about an hour:
- U-insert: about 10 min to swap. The arm and plug come off, the cap does not.
- Pinion-shaft: about 15 min (cap off).
- Gear-spindle and clutch disc: about 10 min (arm off, plug out).

The clutch teeth wear only while slipping. The magnets and washer do not wear.

Before building the robot, run an endurance test: a printed pair, insert and spindle in a printed fixture with a servo, 10^4-10^5 moves, measuring the backlash every 10^4.
r.strength:
All by hand (calc_b2.py, colroom.py, column_b2.py). Allowable 8.5 MPa long-term.

GEAR TEETH (Lewis, rack-generated Y, about 8 % conservative vs Shigley; gear torque = arm-side torque / (1 - spindle friction loss); loss 0.205 at mu 0.15, 0.341 at mu 0.25)

| Case | Lewis stress | With Dolan-Broghamer Kf |
|---|---|---|
| Normal running (arm 4.0 N.mm) | 2.1 MPa | 2.95 MPa |
| Nominal slip 12 N.mm | 6.3 MPa | - |
| Slip at the coin-test upper limit 13.4 N.mm with DRY journals (mu 0.25) | 8.48 MPa | 11.9 MPa |
| Clutch jammed + servo at the 8 % EEPROM limit (27.1 N.mm at the gear) | 11.3 MPa | - |
| Clutch jammed + no torque limit | 142 MPa (teeth break) | - |

- The jammed-clutch case at the 8 % limit is short-term: judged against UTS/2.5 = 12.8 MPa (engineering judgement, not verified for Elegoo Tough).
- Because full stall breaks the teeth, the EEPROM limit is mandatory.
- Contact stress 12 MPa normal, 26 MPa at max slip.
- Torque order: arm need 4.0 < sync sweep <= 6.1 < clutch slip window 9.3-13.4 < gear at 8.5 MPa 20.3 < servo back-up 27.1 (gear side).

SCREW / INSERT JOINTS
- Plug: 3x M2 into glued inserts, same as T4 F8 / v2 (53 N each under L5).
- Spindle-end M2 insert (OD 3.5 x 4, glued): bond shear 5.7 MPa if tightened hard to 0.10 N.m, which is borderline. Tighten gently; the printed hex carries all torque.
- Magnet bond 0.02 MPa; washer bond negligible.
- No screw is used as a shaft or axle.

PRINTED SHAFTS / COUPLER
- Pinion-shaft torsion 1.4 MPa at the 8 % limit; bending at the insert 2.6 MPa at max slip.
- Printed spline bearing 0.9 MPa at the 8 % limit, 11 MPa only at a full-stall fault.
- Spindle land 0.27 MPa at max slip; tongue (solid back) 0.49 MPa.

CLUTCH
- V-tooth bending 0.1 MPa.

PLUG RING under T4 L5 (10 N at the 72 mm tip = 720 N.mm)
- Root D13/6.1: 3.5 MPa (5.3 with Kt 1.5).
- Journal D12.5/6.1: 4.0 MPa (6.0 with Kt 1.5).
- Hub edge load 86 N gives 4.6 MPa contact (rare load).

COLUMN (judge's method: L5, Kt 1.3, column alone)
- Filled legs without steel: <= 5.1 MPa left, <= 7.15 MPa right (z -48.75, beside the J1 cradle). Below the deck: the v2 C-channel, 4.6-4.9 MPa.
- In the real v2 geometry (4-mm-deep strut and narrowed back leg at z -44.5..-26) the stress is 13-18 MPa with or without the v2 rods. The judge's simplified two-leg section hid this; the B2 fill fixes it.
- FE is still required before printing (as for v2).

risks: The wear rate of Elegoo Tough on Tough is unknown (k 1e-5..1e-3). At the worst case the U-insert and teeth add about 5 deg of arm play per year, so parts would need swapping about once a year. Mitigation: graphite/PTFE lubrication, cheap 10-15 min part swaps, an endurance test before the build.

Clutch slip torque before tuning spans 8-18 N.mm (magnet on a thin washer, friction). If it is not tuned into the coin window (9.3-13.4), either the arm slips under its own weight plus light loads, or the teeth exceed 8.5 MPa when the arm is blocked. Mitigation: coin test, 9 tuning combinations.
The printed 20T spline on the metal servo spline may not fit (batch variation). Mitigation: offset coupon; fallback is a trimmed plastic horn bonded into a socket trimmed to r <= 4.7 above z -40.9.
If the EEPROM torque limit is not set (or the servo ignores it) and the clutch jams, full stall breaks the teeth (142 MPa).

SCS0009 at 5 V may give only ~0.19 N.m stall. Then 8 % = 15.2 N.mm, just above the 13.5 N.mm needed at the servo to slip the clutch in the dry case; go to 10 % if needed (the fault-case tooth stress becomes 14.2 MPa).
Arm play from the printed journals: under a push toward the torso at +135 the gap can drop to 0.83-0.91 (rule 1.0 is nominal). Use the +130 deg firmware limit if this matters.

Column: hand calc only, and the fill shape is not yet modelled. The right side is tighter (7.15 MPa); a practical shape below ~85 % of the free section needs the M3x40 fallback. FE is required, as for v2.
Dry resin-on-resin journals may squeak and have higher friction (included up to mu 0.25 in the tooth-stress case); grease compatibility with Tough is unknown.
Print accuracy of m0.65 teeth and the 0.05-0.1 journal clearances depends on the user's printer and resin. Print coupons and a test pair first.

The single-position clutch resync relies on gravity (a free arm hangs or is held below ~30 deg by drag). If a user wedges the arm somewhere, it re-engages only when the drive passes it, which the sync sweep guarantees.

Short-term allowable UTS/2.5 = 12.8 MPa for the jammed-clutch fault case: engineering judgement, no source reachable.
Pull of D4x2 N35 magnets on a 2 mm DIN 9021 washer: ideal-steel model times k_sat 0.6-0.9. Real values come from the coin test.

Fit of a printed 20T internal spline on the metal servo spline (coupon needed).
Printability and accuracy of the m0.65 alpha25 teeth, 0.05-0.1 mm journal clearances and the 30 deg V-teeth on the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K (coupons needed).

judge.winner: B1+ = B1 (printed 12/18 bevel pair, DIN 912 M4x20 arm shaft, MR63/MR74/6700 ball bearings, trimmed-horn coupler, magnetic friction clutch) with 8 judge fixes, merged with the B2 upper-column fill (no rods, no screws in the column). B2 ranked second.
judge.reasons:
RULES CHECK, part by part. Both designs pass (a), (b) and (c).
- B1 bought parts, all used at stock size:
  * SCS0009 (only the plastic ears are cut);
  * the supplied plastic horn (cut and filed; plastic is allowed);
  * MR63ZZ, 2x MR74ZZ and 6700ZZ (common RC / 3D-printing sizes; 6700 is the least common);
  * DIN 912 M4x20 at stock length (caliper selection only; Loctite 638 metal to metal);
  * DIN 125 M10 washer, 5x2 magnets, M2x10 countersunk screws, glued M2 inserts.
  * B1's M3x40 column screw is dropped in the merge.
  * No hidden step, groove, flat, thread or cut length on metal.
- B2 bought parts: servo, M2x10, M2x8, M2 inserts, 4x2 magnets, DIN 9021 M8 washer, epoxy, Loctite 222 and graphite. Shims are cut from paper or PET (not metal). Everything special is printed.

RANKING for this user (buildable + reliable first, then quiet + fewest parts, then look, then cost):
1. B1+ (winner).
   * Every rotating joint runs on ball bearings. There are no resin-on-resin journals.
   * The servo coupling uses the supplied horn, bonded into a printed cup. Research A found this is how hobbyists do it. B2 relies on a printed 20T internal spline pressed onto the metal spline, which is reported as unreliable.
   * Tooth margin on the same basis (tip-direction Lewis x Kf with Kf at rho):
     - B1 pinion: 7.9 MPa at 0.016 N.m and 8.4 MPa at the judge window top of 0.017 N.m.
     - B2: pinion 10.3 and gear 11.2 MPa at its own upper slip (13.4 N.mm with dry journals, which is 20.3 N.mm at the gear). B2's plain-journal friction sits between the clutch and the teeth.
   * The arm is firmer. B1's face preload resists tilt up to 0.8-1.25 N at the tip; B2 resists only 0.2-0.27 N before it shows 0.5-0.9 mm of play.
   * Greased teeth on ball bearings are quieter than dry-graphite resin journals.
2. B2.
   * Fewest and most common parts (6 bought types, no bearings).
   * Positive arm retention (a screw).
   * An elegant single-position self-synchronising clutch.
   * The column fill fixes the inherited overstress of the upper column. This fill is merged into the winner.
   * Against it:
     - plain resin journals (wear k unknown; worst case about 5.6 deg/yr of arm play, possible squeak);
     - spline fit risk;
     - teeth above 8.5 MPa with Kf at its upper slip;
     - pinion top land only 0.15 mm at the toe (B1: 0.25 mm);
     - boss slot cut through the stop ring;
     - the disc screw goes into an insert that is borderline if tightened hard.

B1 DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED (all re-checked):
(1) No inward axial stop for the M4 shaft. Both MR74 outer races slip in the D7 bore, and only A2 has an outboard shoulder.
   * Two loads go straight into the mesh: the drive-hub press-on at every arm refit (14-54 N for 0.02-0.05 interference), and arm pushes up to the magnet force (6-9 N).
   * A 9 N wedge equals about 3.3x the design tooth load, about 28 MPa at the pinion root.
   * B1's claim "the shaft never sees an inward force" is false.
   * Fix: epoxy A2's outer race against the shoulder, and reduce the press fit to 0.02 interference (about 14-22 N, at most 0.25 C0 of the MR74).
(2) Gear on a plain D4.1 bore on a thread: radial runout up to about 0.1 mm closes the 0.08 backlash. Fix: printed M4 internal thread in the gear (flank-centred, epoxied).
(3) Homing.
   * The 3 % stall homing is doubtful.
   * One stop cannot recover an arm that was turned upward by hand by more than 14 deg: the friction clutch holds any offset, and the drive spare is only 14 deg.
   * Fix: a two-sided hidden stop (lug sector widened to 135.8 deg, contacts at -51 and +140.5) and a deterministic two-sweep slip homing at the normal torque limit.
(4) The coin window 0.0136-0.016 is too narrow for magnet-count steps. Fix: window 0.0124-0.0170 plus printed 0.2/0.4 spacers under magnets.
(5) The DIN 125 thickness tolerance (about +-0.2) shifts the arm axially. Fix: bond the washer with its friction face flush to a reference.
(6) The M4 head position is undefined while the glue cures. Fix: printed 0.5 gauge.
(7) The 5.3 boss/plug slot leaves only a 0.69 wall to the glued M2 inserts. Fix: 5.1 (0.60 to the pinion crown).
(8) The upper column is overstressed (22-23 MPa reproduced). Fix: B2 fill with B1 keep-outs; hand check max 5.10 L / 7.15 R MPa with no steel.
