recheck.my_number: 20.4 N.mm and 8.48 MPa on B2's raw basis; 22.5 N.mm on the tip-direction basis. With Kf: pinion 10.3, gear 11.2 MPa (above 8.5 with Kf). B2's friction loss 0.341 reproduced by hand (about 0.33)

recheck.claim: B2 pinion tip thickness 0.37 m (adequate)
recheck.my_number: Top land 0.231 mm at the heel and 0.149 mm at the toe (B1: 0.249 at the toe). B2's toe is fragile

recheck.claim: B1 sweep clearances L/R: coupler 1.23/1.60, pinion 1.23/1.61, boss 1.02/1.40, tongue 1.33/1.66
recheck.my_number: chk.py re-run L and R: identical, line by line

recheck.claim: B1 paths: cap tongue 0.47, strut 0.70, servo slide-in 0.30, T_stred lowering >= 0.8 (0.25 at the v2 front-leg sketch)
recheck.my_number: paths.py re-run L and R: identical

recheck.claim: B2 sweep/static/paths (pinion 1.16/1.54, tongue 1.13/1.51, boss 1.02/1.40, lateral insertion 0.57/0.66)
recheck.my_number: Re-run L and R: identical, except the collar now 3.01/3.41. B2's log predates its final collar r 2.7, which gives more clearance

recheck.claim: B1: the M4 shaft never sees an inward force; inward float limited by the backlash
recheck.my_number: False. The press-on at refit (14-54 N) and arm pushes up to 6-9 N load the M4 inward. The outer races have no inward stop, so the gear wedges into the pinion: 9 N gives 11.6 N equivalent tangential load, about 28 MPa. Fixed by bonding A2's outer race

recheck.claim: B1 drive-hub press-off 45-120 N fresh, 13-60 N long term; lifting the robot by an arm (11 N) holds
recheck.my_number: Thin-ring estimate 14-22 N at 0.02 interference (the fixed value; larger fits overload the MR74 axially). Long-term lower (not measured). Do not lift the robot by an arm

recheck.claim: B1 homing at 3 % (0.010 N.m at the arm) below the clutch, with 10 % slip homing as fallback
recheck.my_number: 3 % is unverified on SCS0009. A single stop recovers only offsets of 14 deg or less in the upward direction. Replaced by a two-sided stop: lug2.py gives contact at -51.0 and +140.5, min gap 0.528 over -45..+135. Two-sweep slip homing at the running limit; teeth see at most the clutch torque

recheck.claim: B1 coin window 0.0136 (2E+50c) / 0.0160 (2E+50c+10c), 4-7 magnets
recheck.my_number: Per-magnet slip torque 0.0018-0.0079 N.m (B1 model up to the effective-gap model). The narrow window can fall between counts. Widened to 0.0124 / 0.0170 (2E+20c / 2E+50c+20c): an integer count of 2-9 always fits. Spacer factors 0.72/0.54

recheck.claim: Upper column of v2 at z -33..-30 is 22-23 MPa under L5 (B1); B2 fill gives 5.10 L / 7.15 R
recheck.my_number: Hand recompute at z -30: Z 35.5 mm3, 23.4 MPa. colroom re-run with B1 keep-outs (coupler r 5.0, slide corridor y -1.8..7.8): max 5.10 L / 7.15 R MPa. Voxel-corner clearance to the B1 coupler 0.32; exact cylinder cut r 5.0 specified

recheck.claim: Arm gap unchanged: 3.70 rest, 1.00 at +135, 3.33 at -45
recheck.my_number: armgap rec1 dx -1.0 log: 3.70 / 1.00 / 3.33. New run: 0.947 at +137, 0.862 at +140.5 (top homing stop only)

recheck.claim: B1 vertical shaft does not turn inside the MR63 bore
recheck.my_number: Radial-load friction about 1.1 N.mm vs ZZ bearing drag about 0.1 N.mm, so the inner race follows. Plausible

recheck.claim: B1 pinion D2.5 D-key torsion 4.9 MPa (at 0.0165)
recheck.my_number: About 5.0 MPa at 0.017. This is at the shear allowable (0.577 x 8.5 = 4.9), for rare slip events only; running 2.4 MPa

recheck.claim: B2 arm tip play 0.53-0.89 mm
recheck.my_number: Reproduced. It appears with only 0.2-0.27 N at the tip (magnet hold-down 1.1-1.5 N at r 13.2). B1 threshold 0.83-1.25 N

judge.final_design:
NOVA mini arm drive B1+ (judge-final, R2c). Frame B: mm, Z up, front -Y, robot left +X. LEFT side values; RIGHT = mirror x -> -x (every check was run on both sides). All numbers are also in /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/vyber/final_B1plus.json.

0 LOOK (unchanged from v2)
- Arm at dx -1.0.
- Black plug face recessed 1.0 in the r 14 socket (0.5 seam). Black ring D13 into the arm's D14 hole.
- Gap 3.70 at rest, >= 1.00 over -45..+135 (1.00 at +135), 3.33 at -45. During homing only: 0.86 at +140.5.
- Visible hardware: the 3 countersunk M2 heads on the recessed plug face, largely behind the arm.

1 SERVO + COLUMN (T_spodok)
- SCS0009 earless, standing, output up on (39, 3). Case x 32.95..45.05, y -14.3..8.9, top face z -45.0.
- The official drawing gives 25.25 to the top face, so the bottom is at -70.25. Measure the servo, then set the pad and the coupler depth (open item).
- v2 pocket column, kept:
  * C-channel below the deck, web, pad, printed snap tab, cable slot in the front leg, F3a_2 at (29.5, 4.0).
  * Optional thin felt tape against rattle.
- No steel rods and no screws in the column. The upper legs are filled into the free space for z -49..-27 (B2 fill), in the bands y 7.5..16.5 and y -21..-9, x down to about 31.5. Keep-outs:
  * cylinder r 5.0 about (39, 3) for z -44..-35 (B1 coupler);
  * slab y -1.8..7.8 for x >= 34.2, z -44..-35 (coupler slide-in path);
  * r 3.0 above z -35 (lifted shaft);
  * the T_bok removal path;
  * >= 1.0 to the pan/lift sweep;
  * >= 0.5 to the T_stred path;
  * trim 0.1 at the T_paluba edge.
- Hand check (L5, Kt 1.3, column alone): max 5.10 L / 7.15 R MPa. FE is still required.

2 VERTICAL DRIVE
- Coupler: printed cup r 4.5, z -43.5..-35.5.
  * The supplied single-arm horn (hub D7.4 x 4.1) is bonded inside with 2K epoxy: arm cut off, two flats filed to AF 6.2.
  * A shoulder above the hub, so pressing pushes on the horn, not through the bond.
  * Hex socket 4 AF at the top. The horn screw is driven through the socket.
  * Fallback if no horn is in the box: a printed 20T internal spline from a coupon (OD 3.95 / root 3.45; offsets 0/+0.02/+0.04/+0.06).
- Vertical shaft (printed, one piece, axis vertical):
  * hex 4 AF at z -39.6..-36.1, hand press into the coupler;
  * D3 journal at -36.1..-23.43, through the D4 tongue hole and the MR63ZZ;
  * D2.5 D-key at -23.43..-20.47.
- MR63ZZ (3x6x2.5): outer race epoxied in the v2 tongue ring r 3.0..4.4, z -26.35..-23.85.
- Pinion 12T (printed):
  * slips on the D-key and sits on a printed shim (r 1.55..1.9; 0.30/0.42/0.50/0.60, nominal 0.42) on the MR63 inner race;
  * back face relieved 0.2 over r 1.95..3.6;
  * held down by the mesh thrust.
- Service lift 4.5 (plug out): shaft and pinion rise together into the boss slot (toe -15.97 vs roof -15.5); the hex leaves the coupler by 0.4.

3 GEAR PAIR (printed Elegoo Tough, straight bevel)
- Sigma 90, apex O (39, 3, -17).
- z 12/18, m 0.6667 at the heel, PA 25, ha* 0.9, hf* 1.15, rack tip radius 0.38m, x 0, b 2.8.
- R 7.211, delta 33.69/56.31, ratio 1.5, eps 1.29.
- Pinion: toe z -20.467 r 2.752; crown z -22.667 r 4.499; heel root z -23.425.
- Gear: toe x 41.141 r 3.874; crown x 42.501 r 6.333; root x 43.638; back x 44.238 (relieved to 44.038 for r > 3).
- Gear bore: printed M4x0.7 internal thread (0.1 radial clearance). It is screwed onto the M4 and epoxied, so it centres on the flanks.
- Thin each flank 0.02 for backlash. Do not leave sharp tips (form vs active-profile margin is only about 0.02 mm).
- Print axis vertical, 20 um layers, supports on the back faces only.
- Lubricant on the teeth: PTFE grease or graphite, after a 3-7 day test on scrap.

4 PLUG CARTRIDGE zatka_L/P (black Tough, printed on its axis)
- Outside as v2: neck r 11 (x 38.6..40.6), body r 13.5, face recessed 1.0, ring D13 to x 52.5.
- Fixing:
  * 3x M2x10 countersunk at r 9.0 (12/4/8 o'clock) into epoxied M2 brass inserts in the boss;
  * 2 printed pegs D2.4 at r 9.0 (10 and 2 o'clock).
- Inside:
  * gear cavity r 6.9 to x 44.54;
  * 6 o'clock slot |y-3| <= 5.1 for x < 44.0 (the boss slot is also 5.1);
  * D7 bore x 44.54..55.10 with the outboard shoulder at 55.10;
  * seat D10 x 52.5..59.5, bore D5.0 outboard of 55.1.
- Stop lug on the seat: x 52.5..55.0, r 5.0..6.6, sector azimuth 247.8..383.5 deg (135.8 deg wide; azimuth 0 = +Y, 90 = +Z).
- Bearings:
  * A2 = MR74ZZ at x 52.60..55.10. Outer race epoxied against the shoulder (inward and outward axial stop).
  * Printed spacer sleeve D7/D5.
  * A1 = MR74ZZ at x 44.54..47.04, outer race slip.
- Arm shaft = DIN 912 M4x20 8.8, major diameter >= 3.93:
  * shank x 40.0..60.0; head x 60.0..64.0, set 0.5 off the seat end with a printed gauge while curing;
  * A1/A2 inner races Loctite 638 + activator on the thread;
  * 0.30 shim between the gear back and the A1 inner race fixes the mounting distance.
- Thrust paths: outward gear thrust goes A1 -> spacer -> A2 -> shoulder. Inward loads (arm refit, pushes) go into A2's bond, never into the teeth.

5 ARM SIDE (inside the arm, dx -1.0)
- 6700ZZ: outer race epoxied in the printed arm hub (bore D15, x 55.5..59.5); inner race slip on the D10 seat.
- Arm hub:
  * rib x 53..55, r 5.5..8.5, 32.7 deg wide, at azimuth 180.4 deg at rest;
  * flange x 59.6..60.6;
  * cavity r 11.5, wall r 11.5..12.7 to x 67.6;
  * printed lip ring x 66.4..67.6, inner r 10.4, bonded.
- Washer DIN 125 M10 (10.5x20x2) at r 5.25..10, x 60.6..62.6. Bonded with its friction face flush to a reference (hub face down on glass); the epoxy takes up the thickness tolerance.
- Drive hub (printed, captive between washer and lip):
  * pocket over the M4 head x 60..64, 0.02 diametral interference by coupon;
  * printed hex 3 AF key in the socket;
  * boss r 4.5;
  * disc r 11.0 at x 62.6..65.9, friction face = 0.25 skin printed face down;
  * 8 pockets D5.1 at r 7.7, open outboard, depth 3.05;
  * NdFeB 5x2 N38 axial magnets, alternating polarity, typically 4-7. Fine tuning with printed 0.2/0.4 spacers under the magnets (force x 0.72 / x 0.54).
- Clutch: preload is the magnet pull, an internal loop (no spring, no bearing preload). Faces dry and degreased.
  * Window at the arm: 0.0124-0.0170 N.m.
  * Coin test, arm forward-horizontal, servo holding, coins at 60 mm from the axis: 2 EUR + 20 c (14.24 g) must HOLD; 2 EUR + 50 c + 20 c (22.04 g) must SLIP.
- Two-sided hidden stop: the rib meets the lug at -51.0 deg (0.576 at -45) and at +140.5 deg (0.528 at +135).
- Arm on/off: arm cover off, firm straight pull. Re-fit at the hanging pose: rotate until the hex key drops in, then push.

6 FIRMWARE
- Running torque limit 15 % (above the clutch, so the clutch alone caps the teeth). 65 C. Range -45..+135. Limit acceleration so the dynamic torque stays <= 0.004 N.m.
- Homing at power-up and after any unexpected load peak:
  1. slow sweep to the servo low end (the arm stops at -51, the clutch slips);
  2. slow sweep to the high end (the arm stops at +140.5, the clutch slips).
  * The offset is then known: about 4.25 deg spare at each end.
  * Needs servo travel >= 287 deg (SCS0009 nominal 300; check on the bench).
  * No low-torque stall detection is needed; the teeth never see more than the clutch torque.

7 ASSEMBLY (as v2/B1)
- Bench:
  1. Epoxy MR63 in the tongue, A2 in the plug, and the inserts in the boss; let it cure.
  2. Spacer and A1 into the bore.
  3. M4 through from outboard with 638 on the bearing zones; 0.5 gauge under the head.
  4. 0.30 shim and gear screwed on from the cavity side, with epoxy in the thread.
- Torso:
  1. Shaft up through the MR63 from below.
  2. Pinion and shim on top.
  3. Lift the shaft 4.5.
  4. Slide the servo (with the coupler on its spline) in along -X.
  5. Lower the hex into the coupler.
  6. Fit the cap (v2 notch passes the shaft).
  7. Fit the plug: pegs, 3x M2 snug.
  8. Check for no tight spot over the full range; set the backlash with the pinion shim.
  9. Grease the teeth.
  10. Arm on, then the cover.
  11. Home, then the coin test.
- Servo swap about 10 min: arm cover, arm off, 3 screws, plug out, cap off, lift the shaft, servo out along +X.

8 RIGHT SIDE
- Mirror x -> -x. The web is the J1 cradle end wall, as in v2. Servo to J1 cradle 0.56; coupler/pinion to the sweep 1.60/1.61. Column fill R max 7.15 MPa.

user_operations: Vytlačiť skúšobné kupóny z Elegoo Tough: čap Ø3 do MR63, otvor Ø7 pre MR74, sedlo Ø10 pre 6700, šesťhran 4 AF do spojky, nalisovanie unášača na hlavu M4 (presah 0,01 / 0,02 / 0,03), kožu 0,25 mm; vybrať varianty, ktoré sedia.
Vytlačiť skúšobný pár koliesok 12/18 a pretočiť ho rukou (odporúčaný je aj skúšobný beh 10⁴–10⁵ pohybov).

Vytlačiť všetky diely (spojka, zvislý hriadeľ, pastorok, koleso so závitom M4, podložky, dištančné puzdro, čierna zátka, unášač, náboj ruky, krúžok, rozpierky pod magnety, kaliber 0,5 mm), umyť a vytvrdiť.
Servo: bočnými štípačkami odstrihnúť plastové úšká a zabrúsiť; zmerať skutočnú výšku serva.

Páčka: odstrihnúť rameno plastovej páčky, pilníkom zapilovať dve plôšky na 6,2 mm, vlepiť ju 2K epoxidom do tlačenej spojky; spojku natlačiť (cez páčku) na drážkovanie serva a cez šesťhranný otvor zaskrutkovať dodanú skrutku.
Posuvným meradlom vybrať skrutky M4×20 s priemerom závitu aspoň 3,93 mm.
Zátka na stole: vonkajší krúžok ložiska MR74 (A2) vlepiť 2K epoxidom do otvoru Ø7 až na doraz a nechať vytvrdnúť; potom vložiť dištančné puzdro a druhé MR74 (A1) voľne.
Natrieť Loctite 638 s aktivátorom na závit M4 v miestach ložísk, zasunúť skrutku zvonka cez A2 a A1 a pod hlavu vložiť tlačený kaliber 0,5 mm.
Z dutiny nasadiť podložku 0,30 a naskrutkovať koleso 18 z (tenká vrstva epoxidu v závite) až na podložku, držať, kým lepidlo stuhne; potom kaliber vybrať.
Vonkajší krúžok MR63 vlepiť epoxidom do jazýčka v T_spodok; 3 mosadzné vložky M2 vlepiť 2K epoxidom do nálitku.
Náboj ruky: vlepiť ložisko 6700 vonkajším krúžkom; podložku M10 odmastiť a vlepiť tak, aby jej trecia plocha ležala na skle (zarovno s referenciou); vložiť unášač a nalepiť krúžok.
Magnety 5×2: overiť, že sú magnetované axiálne, vložiť 6 ks so striedavou polaritou do vreciek unášača (kvapka lepidla).

Montáž v trupe: zvislý hriadeľ zdola cez MR63, navrch pastorok s podložkou 0,42, hriadeľ nadvihnúť o 4,5 mm, servo so spojkou zasunúť pozdĺž −X, hriadeľ spustiť a šesťhran zatlačiť rukou do spojky, nasadiť bočný kryt.
Vložiť zátku (2 kolíky do otvorov) a jemne dotiahnuť 3 skrutky M2×10, bez zaisťovača.

Steel D3 h6 vertical shaft with a D-flat replaced by a printed shaft: hex 4 AF / D3 journal / D2.5 D-key. The pinion slips on the key and sits on a printed shim on the MR63 (no glue).

Turned D4/D3 steel arm shaft (tapped end, e-clip) replaced by a stock DIN 912 M4x20. The MR74 inner races are bonded on the thread with Loctite 638. JUDGE: A2's outer race is epoxied against the shoulder, giving an inward axial stop.

Homing: v2's hidden pin stop and 15 % stall replaced by a two-sided hidden stop. The rib in the arm hub meets a 135.8 deg lug on the plug seat at -51 and +140.5 (JUDGE). Homing is two slow sweeps at the running limit; no low-torque stall needed.

The D2 h6 dowels are replaced by printed D2.4 pegs. Plug cavity r 6.9. Boss and plug slots |y-3| <= 5.1 (v2 5.0, B1 5.3).
Column: the D3 silver-steel rods (cut to length) and B1's M3x40 are removed. The upper legs are filled into the free space (B2 fill with B1 keep-outs): hand check 5.10 L / 7.15 R MPa.

T_bok_L and T_bok_P: inner notch x +-39.0..41.2, |y-3| <= 2.0, z -33.5..-27.5 (v2); exterior unchanged.

judge.arm_gap:
Unchanged from v2, because no visible part moves.
- Plug face recessed 1.0 in the r 14 socket. Black D13 ring into the arm's D14 hole. Arm at dx -1.0.
- Judge armgap (rec1, dx -1.0): 3.70 mm at rest (cap rim near (49.3, 1.4, -30.9)), 1.15 at +130, 1.00 at +135, 3.33 at -45.
- New run for the homing excursion only: 0.947 at +137 and 0.862 at +140.5. The arm stops there on the hidden top stop and never touches the torso.
- Axial stack: plug shoulder -> bonded A2 (bearing play +-0.025) -> M4 head set with the 0.5 gauge (+-0.03) -> drive-hub pocket (+-0.03) -> washer face referenced flush (its thickness tolerance is taken by the epoxy) -> arm hub. That is about +-0.08, so the +135 gap is 0.92-1.08.
- Check after assembly: arm skin to plug face on the axis 3.9 +- 0.1. Correct with the drive-hub pocket depth, not with the gear shim.
- B2 for comparison: same nominal gap, but under a push of only 0.2-0.3 N it closes to 0.83-0.91 at +135, from journal play.
judge.noise:
* **Gear mesh.** One added mesh: a resin-on-resin straight bevel pair, greased.
  * At most about 0.25-0.75 rev/s at the pinion, so 3-9 Hz mesh frequency and no tonal whine.
  * Polymer teeth damp impacts better than the v2 brass pair.
  * The SCS0009's own metal gear train stays the dominant sound.
* **Bearings.** All rotating joints are greased ball bearings. There are no dry resin journals that could squeak; B2 has those.
* **Clutch.**
  * Silent in normal running.
  * A slip is a soft scrape with no detents, because the washer is uniform.
  * At power-up homing it scrapes briefly twice, about 8 deg at each hidden stop.
* **Other parts.** No rattling parts: the pinion is held by its own thrust, the drive hub is pressed on, and felt tape is optional on the servo pocket.
* Noise was not measured; this is a qualitative estimate.
judge.durability:
**Teeth.**
- Running stress (0.008 N.m) is 2.8 MPa (Lewis) and 4.0 MPa with Kf, below the 6 MPa cyclic target.
- No sustained load: the arm rests at 0 deg, where the gravity torque is zero.
- Slip events (rare) reach at most 5.9 / 8.4 MPa.
- Wear is unverified. B1's Archard estimate (k 1e-5, +-10x) is 0.3-1.5 deg of extra backlash per 1e7 engagements. My order-of-magnitude estimate is about 0.06 mm of flank wear per year at k 1e-4 for heavy use.
- The pinion wears first. Swap: plug out (3 screws), new pinion on the D-key; about 15 min plus printing.
- The gear is replaced together with a new M4x20. A2 is bonded, so a gear swap may also need a new plug print or a reused bearing freed with heat.

**Creep.** No resin part carries a permanent preload.
- The clutch force is magnetic and closes internally between the drive hub and the washer.
- The plug screws are snug only.
- The drive-hub press fit relaxes; this lowers only the breakaway force. Reprint the hub 0.01 tighter if the arm comes off too easily (maximum 0.03, MR74 axial limit).

**Clutch.**
- Face pressure 0.05 MPa; about 2-5 mm of sliding per homing. Wear is negligible.
- If the skin wears, the magnet force rises slightly, so the slip torque cannot fall below the window over life.
- The friction coefficient can drift. Repeat the coin test once a year and change magnets or spacers if needed.

**Bearings.** MR63/MR74/6700 run far below their ratings.
- The inner races follow their shafts, because radial friction is greater than bearing drag.
- The 6700 inner race only slides axially, and only at arm fitting.

**Stops.** The rib in the arm hub is the sacrificial part.
- 1.3 MPa at the clutch torque.
- 16 MPa at a 3 N tip push past the stop (short-term).
- About 54 MPa at 10 N, which dents it. The arm hub is a cheap reprint.

**Print drift.** Coupons are needed for the D3 in the MR63, the D7 bore, the D10 seat, the hex fits, the drive-hub press, the 0.25 skin and the 20 um teeth.
judge.strength:
Judge numbers: gear_judge.py, judge_calc.py, plus B1's strength_b1.py where noted. Allowable 8.5 MPa long term.

**Teeth** (tip-direction Lewis / x Kf at rho):
- Pinion at 0.004 N.m: 1.38 / 1.98 MPa.
- At 0.008 N.m: 2.76 / 3.96 MPa.
- At the clutch window top 0.017 N.m: 5.86 / 8.41 MPa.
- Gear at 0.017: 4.69 / 7.27 MPa.
- Allowable arm torque 0.0246 (Lewis) / 0.0172 (with Kf). The clutch caps the teeth for any servo setting.
- B2 at its own slip limit: 10.3 / 11.2 MPa with Kf.

**Vertical drive** at 0.017 N.m at the arm:
- D2.5 D-key torsion about 5.0 MPa (at the shear allowable, slip events only); running 2.4.
- D3 bending at the MR63 4.6 MPa.
- Coupler hex 0.45 MPa; horn flats 0.39 MPa.

**Arm shaft and joints:**
- M4 steel bending under a sideways push 36 MPa (B1). A printed D4 would see 18.7.
- Gear thread epoxy about 0.2 MPa; 638 on the races 0.37 MPa.
- A2 outer-race epoxy under the refit press (<= 30 N): 0.55 MPa.
- MR74 axial load at refit 14-22 N, below 0.25 C0 (27 N).
- Drive-hub pocket edge 5.1 MPa; hex key 1.2 MPa.

**Without the A2 fix** (as B1 was submitted): a 9 N inward push wedges the mesh to about 28 MPa at the pinion root, and a refit press of 30 N reaches about 93 MPa.

**Clutch:** per magnet 0.93-2.6 N through the skin (B1 model to judge upper estimate); slip torque per magnet 0.0018-0.0079 N.m; face pressure 0.05 MPa.

**Homing stop:** 1.3 MPa at the clutch torque (contact 2.2 mm2 at r 6.05). Lug root shear 3.2 MPa at a 3 N tip push.

**Plug under L5** (0.72 N.m): seat D10/D5 7.8 MPa (9.4 with Kt 1.2), the same as v2 and above 8.5 for this rare abuse case. The 135.8 deg lug stiffens the seat root; FE pending. Ring D13/D7 root 4.7 MPa.

**Column under L5** (Kt 1.3, column alone):
- C-channel below the deck 2.6-4.9 MPa.
- Filled upper legs max 5.10 L / 7.15 R MPa (z -27.25 L, z -48.75 R).
- The v2 section without the fill is 23.4 MPa at z -30 (reproduced).
- FE including the side cap is still required.
open_items: Servo height: the official SC09 drawing gives 25.25 mm to the top face (21.45 to the body shoulder) and 3.2 mm of spline above it. The v2 pocket modelled 21.5. Measure the real servo, then set the pad (bottom about z -70.25 if the top face stays at -45) and the coupler cup depth. This clashes with the relocated buck converter under the left pocket (top <= -70.85, x up to 38.4), so the buck needs a new place. Inherited from v2; it affects both designs.

FE of T_spodok (column with the merged fill, boss, tongue) and of the plug seat under L5, including the side-cap load share. The hand checks are 5.1 / 7.15 MPa for the column and 7.8-9.4 MPa at the plug seat.

Endurance test of a printed 12/18 pair before the build: 1e4-1e5 moves at the clutch torque, measuring backlash every 1e4. Also check grease compatibility with Elegoo Tough on scrap for 3-7 days. No wear or fatigue data exists for MSLA Tough gears.
Servo travel must be >= 287 deg for the two-stop homing (SCS0009 nominal 300 deg). Check on the bench. If it is shorter, move the top stop down and limit the range (for example +130).

Real magnet force through the 0.25 skin and the friction coefficient on the zinc washer. Estimates span 0.93-2.6 N per magnet and mu 0.25-0.4. Settled by the coin test, the magnet count (2-9) and the printed spacers.
Drive-hub press fit on the knurled M4 head: retention force and relaxation are not measured. Coupon 0.01/0.02/0.03. The arm is a breakaway part; do not lift the robot by an arm.
Horns in the servo box: Waveshare's package list says 'servo only'. If no horn comes, use the printed 20T internal-spline coupon in the same cup.

6700ZZ is the least common bought part. No Slovak shop was confirmed (Bambu Lab EU EA032, Robitronic RC1015, loziska-policka.cz, bike shops). A printed journal as in B2 would remove it, but needs a seat, lug and rib rework that has not been checked.
All shop availability and prices come from search snippets (verified=false). Shop hosts were not reachable from the session.
Elegoo Tough material data (E about 2 GPa, UTS 29-32 MPa) comes from listings, not a TDS. No creep or fatigue data.

Tooth geometry was checked only as 2-D virtual spur gears: Lewis, Kf, contact ratio, form vs active profile with about 0.02 mm margin. No 3-D tooth mesh interference or transmission-error check. Keep the tips slightly rounded.
SC09 cable exit end decides which leg gets the cable slot. With no column screw any more, this no longer conflicts with anything.
D2.5 D-key torsion about 5.0 MPa at clutch slip sits at the shear allowable. It is acceptable for rare slips; if the test pair shows trouble, make the pinion bore D2.8 (toe wall 0.65).

The image pipeline (/tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R1/img_v2/work/parts_v2.py) still models v2. It must be updated to the B1+ parts: printed pair, M4 shaft, threaded gear, bonded A2, 135.8 deg lug, magnet drive hub, washer, lip ring and column fill.

issues.what: The plug screw 'M2x10 countersunk (DIN 965 PH or DIN 7991)' has two problems. DIN 7991 has no M2 size. And one length for all three screws gives very uneven thread engagement, with one tip going out through the back of the boss.
issues.evidence:
DIN 7991 / ISO 10642 start at M3; this is from the standard and was not web-checked. My calculation uses the v2 geometry, which B1+ keeps: screw circle r 9.0, plug face = torso surface − 1.0, boss x 34.4..38.4.
- 12 o'clock (y 3.0, z −8.0): face at x 43.69. An M2x10 tip lands at x 33.69, so 4.71 mm sits in the boss and the tip sticks out 0.71 mm behind the 4 mm boss, into space nobody has checked.
- 4 o'clock (y 10.79, z −21.5): face at 45.54; 2.86 mm engaged.
- 8 o'clock (y −4.79, z −21.5): face at 46.49; only 1.91 mm engaged (about 4 threads in a 4 mm insert).
The log is in overenie_nakup/evidence.json. The Hornbach 'M2x10 PH countersunk 30 pcs' listing is not confirmed.

Use a different standard length at each position: M2x8 at 12 o'clock (2.7 mm engaged), M2x10 at 4 o'clock (2.9 mm), M2x12 at 8 o'clock (3.9 mm, tip at x 34.49, still inside the boss). The right side is the same at the same (y, z) positions. Re-check these values on the B1+ T_spodok boss and the insert depth. Alternatively, keep one length and adjust the boss and insert depth per hole.

issues.what: The arm shaft DIN 912 M4x20 is a standard size, but three things the design relies on are not guaranteed: the shop listing, a thread diameter of at least 3.93, and the head diameter that the 0.02 press fit assumes.
issues.evidence:
ISO 4762 (from the standard, not web-checked):
- For M4, b = 20, so l = 20 is threaded to the head. The incomplete thread runs out within about 2P = 1.4 mm under the head, and A2 sits 4.9 mm or more from the head, so 'fully threaded' is fine.
- The 6g major diameter can be 3.838 to 3.978. A pack of 15 may hold no screw at 3.93 or above.
- Head diameter is 6.78 to 7.00 for a plain head and up to 7.22 for a knurled head, which is much wider than the 0.01/0.02/0.03 coupon steps.
The 'Hornbach 15-pack, product 12663705' was not seen. The saved snippets show only M3 DIN 912 at Hornbach CZ (prieskum_zelezarstvo/notes.md).
issues.fix: Confirm a shop listing. Buy two packs, for example 8.8 zinc and 12.9 black; 12.9 black is also fine for Loctite 638 and the press fit. State a fallback if no screw reaches 3.93 (for example accept 3.90 and rely on the gear's flank-centred thread), and say whether that is allowed. Measure the head diameter of the chosen screw with calipers and print the drive-hub coupon as that measured value minus 0.01/0.02/0.03, not from nominal 7.0. Say what to do with a knurled head: the pocket bore must be sized to the knurl crest.

issues.what: The clutch washer DIN 125 M10 can be bought wrong (stainless), and its punching burr could force metal work.
issues.evidence: The magnetic clutch only works on a ferromagnetic washer. Hardware stores stock M10 washers in A2 stainless as often as in zinc-plated steel, and A2 is practically non-magnetic. The Slovak shopping list says only 'oceľ pozinkovaná' (zinc-plated steel), with no warning. Punched DIN 125 washers have a burr on one face; sanding it off would be grinding metal, which rule (a) forbids. No shop page for it was opened, though the item itself is a standard part.

In the assembly step, add: 'trecia plocha = hladká strana bez otrepu; stranu s otrepom vlepiť do drážky, nič nebrúsiť' (the friction face is the smooth, burr-free side; glue the burr side into the recess; do not grind anything).

checked: The user operations list contains no metal work, so rule (a) passes. The operations are: cutting the servo's plastic ears; cutting and filing the plastic horn; measuring screws with calipers; Loctite 638 and epoxy bonding; pressing the drive hub onto the M4 head; screwing the printed gear onto the M4; gluing in brass inserts; magnets; coin test. Nothing is cut, drilled, tapped, turned, ground or bent in metal. Freeing a bonded bearing with heat (durability text) is not metal work. One gap: the washer burr needs a 'do not sand' rule, raised as an issue.

Every screw length is a stock length; nothing is cut. DIN 912 M4x20 is a standard length and, per ISO 4762 (b = 20 for M4), threaded to the head, so the design's 'fully threaded' is right. The A2 seat at x 52.6..55.1 is at least 4.9 mm from the head, outside the ≤1.4 mm thread run-out. The screw tip at x 40.0 is 1.6 mm from the boss face. The gear thread at x 41.14..44.24 lies on full thread.

M2x10 is a standard DIN 965 length, but the computed engagement is uneven: 4.71 / 2.86 / 1.91 mm at 12 / 4 / 8 o'clock, with the 12 o'clock tip 0.71 mm past the boss (raised as an issue). M2x8 and M2x12 are also standard DIN 965 lengths. This comes from the standard, not the web.

issues.what: The coin calibration of the clutch cannot be done as written. Coins are to be taped 60 mm from the shoulder axis, but no point of the arm is that far out. The window arithmetic also uses an arm gravity torque about twice my estimate.
issues.evidence: v_arm.py/json (T3 pebble placed with armgeo, dx -1.0): the arm surface reaches at most 53.75 mm from the shoulder axis (tip at (71.46, 0.23, -70.68)). Coins with 22-26 mm diameter cannot be centred beyond about 45-50 mm. The area-weighted shell centroid is 14.75 mm from the axis, so a 13 g shell gives 0.0019 N.m when horizontal (0.0022 at 15 g), not the 0.004 used. The window 0.0124/0.0170 equals coin torque at 60 mm (0.00838/0.01297) + 0.004. With the real arm torque and a reachable lever of about 48 mm, the same coins give about 0.0086/0.0123. The clutch setting is the only protection for the teeth and the stop rib, and as specified it cannot be measured.
issues.fix: Redefine the test at a reachable radius, or use a printed clip-on lever or a hook with a defined radius. Use the computed arm torque (about 0.002 N.m, ideally weighed and balanced on the real arm). Recompute the coin combinations for the corrected (and preferably lowered) window. Update the Slovak user text.

issues.what: On the left side, the merged column fill (colfill_B1merge_L.npz) sits above the trimmed T_paluba deck. The deck can then no longer be lowered into place (assembly step T3, straight down along -Z).

issues.what: The column hand check (5.10 L / 7.15 R MPa) leaves out the torsion from the off-axis L5 tip load. With torsion included, the back leg of the column alone is far above 8.5 MPa, so fix (8) is not demonstrated.

At +135 deg it sits at y -35.0, z 21.0: My 380 and Mz 380 N.mm at the shoulder. At +90 deg: Mz 538 N.mm. Torsion is taken as an x-shear couple V = Mz/d (d 27.4) in the legs. Kt 1.3.
- +135 deg, L: back leg 11.0 (top-free bound) to 19.2 (fixed-guided bound) MPa at z -28.25 (leg Z 32.4 mm3).
- +135 deg, R: 13.2 to 23.5 MPa.
- +90 deg: L 9.9 to 21.6, R 12.4 to 26.9 MPa.
- Without torsion my per-leg values are 4.7 L / 6.0 R, which agrees with the judge. The judge's moment arm (33.9 - z) is conservative for bending but adds no torsion.
- Not included: the side cap's share (unknown).
issues.fix: Do not print T_spodok before an FE run that applies the full shoulder load (Fx, My and Mz, arm at +90 and +135) with the side cap. Alternatively, tie the legs together in torsion, for example with a plate between the legs at z -44..-41 for x <= 34, where the sweep envelope is only r 26.5; check that against the servo, coupler and T5 paths. The back leg at z -30..-27 needs about 3x its current section modulus.

issues.what: The vertical shaft and pinion are located axially in more than one place, so the backlash shim can be overridden.
issues.evidence:
From final_B1plus.json:
- The shaft hex bottom (-39.6) sits on the coupler socket floor (-39.6).
- The shaft's D3/D2.5 step (-23.43) is at the same height as the pinion back face and the top of the 0.42 shim (-23.43). The step faces up, so the pinion rests on whichever is higher, the shim or the step.
- If the coupler sits higher (horn bonding, spline end-play) or the horn screw head stands above the floor (head top about -39.2 if the horn hub top is near -40.8), the step lifts the pinion off the shim. The 0.517 mm of backlash per mm of pinion lift (v_gear.json) means a 0.17 mm rise uses up the whole 0.088 mm nominal backlash and the mesh binds.
- The 0.30 shim (top -23.55) can never take effect while the shaft rests on the floor.
issues.fix: Move the D3->D2.5 step to about z -24.0 (2.35 of the 2.5 mm bearing length stays on the D3 journal), so that the shim alone sets the pinion height for every shim from 0.30 to 0.60. Deepen the socket floor by 0.6 mm and add a 1.5 mm relief in the hex end for the horn screw head. Check that the horn screw head passes the 4 AF socket (inscribed diameter 4.0); if not, use 5 AF.

issues.what: The tooth margin at the clutch slip torque is about zero, and below zero with a normal load-distribution factor. The required order clutch < tooth limit is therefore not met robustly. The same slip happens at every power-up homing, so it is not rare. The D-key also sits at its shear limit at every homing.
issues.evidence:
v_gear.py/json, my own rack generator. It reproduces Y 0.398/0.498, Kf 1.405/1.550 and eps 1.291.
- At 0.0170 N.m on the arm: pinion 5.87 MPa (Lewis), 8.25 MPa (x Kf), 10.31 MPa (x Kf x Km 1.25).
- Allowable arm torque at 8.5 MPa: 0.0175 (x Kf), 0.0140 (Km 1.25), 0.0117 (Km 1.5).
- Km 1.25 is the AGMA 2003 value for straight bevels with neither member straddle-mounted. Here the pinion overhangs a single 2.5 mm MR63, and a 0.5 deg shaft-angle error alone gives 0.024 mm mismatch across the 2.8 mm face, more than the 0.02 per-flank thinning.
- The window top 0.0170 is only 3% below 0.0175.
- The skin wear argued in the design pushes the slip torque up, beyond the window.
- D2.5 D-key: 5.0 MPa nominal against a 4.9 MPa shear allowable, plus the stress concentration at the flat, at every homing.
issues.fix: Lower the clutch window to about 0.008-0.0115 N.m at the arm. The real gravity torque is about 0.002, so dynamic torque <= 0.004 still holds with margin. That gives the pinion about 7 MPa even with Km 1.25. Alternatively make the teeth larger, or the D-key D2.8 or a hex key. State the margin with Km in the user text.

issues.what: The pinion involute ends only 0.02-0.04 mm below where the gear tip starts contact (form radius vs SAP). Setting backlash by shimming the mesh deeper therefore drives the gear tip into the pinion root fillet.
issues.evidence:
v_gear.json: pinion SAP 6.632 m vs form radius 6.575 m (0.057 m).
- Margin: 0.038 mm at the heel, 0.031 at the mean section, 0.023 at the toe.
- A deeper normal approach of 0.069 mm at the toe (0.091 at the mean section) uses it up; this equals a backlash reduction of 0.064-0.085 mm.
- Printed teeth 0.02 mm/flank thinner than nominal (j +0.088), corrected with the pinion shim, put the gear tip into the trochoid.
- The design only says 'do not leave sharp tips'.
issues.fix: Design in a tip relief: gear ha* 0.8 or a 0.1-0.15 mm tip round/chamfer on both members, and re-check the contact ratio (about 1.2). Set backlash first by tooth thickness (thickness coupons) and use the shim only for the mounting-distance stack.

issues.what: The backlash adjustment range is too small for the axial tolerance stack.
issues.evidence:
v_gear.json, backlash_stack:
- Sensitivity: 0.517 mm of transverse backlash per mm of pinion axial move and 0.776 per mm of gear axial move.
- The shim set 0.30/0.42/0.50/0.60 corrects only -0.093..+0.062 mm.
- Stack: shoulder, spacer, gear shim, plug face to shoulder, boss face and cap flange (printed, +-0.05..0.08); MR74 x2 and MR63 widths (0/-0.12); bearing axial play; printed tooth thickness.
- Result: mean shift +0.124, 3-sigma RSS +-0.132, print +-0.088. The correction needed spans about -0.34..+0.10 mm.
- The gear side cannot be adjusted once A2 and the threaded gear are bonded.
- The coarse steps (0.04-0.06 mm of backlash per shim step) are close to the 0.088 nominal backlash.
issues.fix: Print a finer and wider pinion shim set (0.20-0.90 in 0.05 steps). Choose the A1-A2 spacer length (or the gear shim) by measurement before bonding. Give a measured backlash target and a tool-free check (for example a paper strip of known thickness in the mesh).

issues.what: The arm gap has no margin at +135 deg and is below the 1.0 mm moving-part rule at the homing stop. Tolerances and tilt make both worse.
issues.evidence:
v_gap.py, own check against the real T_bok_L and mirrored T_bok_P meshes plus the recessed plug disc. Both sides: 3.702 at rest, 3.333 at -45, 1.153 at 130, 1.001 at 135, 0.947 at 137, 0.862 at 140.5 (reached at every power-up).
- The gap falls about 0.030 mm per degree near 135.
- The axial stack of +-0.08 (judge) moves the >=1.0 limit to about +132 deg.
- Tilt play of 0.0101 rad (0.03 mm seat fit over 4 mm plus 0.15 deg bearing) closes the gap point at r about 14 by about 0.14 mm. Under a push that leaves about 0.78 at +135 and 0.64 at +140.5.
issues.fix: Limit the working range to about +130 deg (gap 1.15) and put the top stop at about +134; or add about 0.2 mm to the arm dx, or trim the cap rim locally. Re-check the two-sided stop angles and the 287 deg servo travel accordingly.

issues.what: The hidden stop rib in the arm hub breaks under a modest hand push. The clutch does not protect the stop: hand torque goes straight into the rib, which conflicts with the 'strong / unbreakable' wish.
issues.evidence:
v_rib.py/json. Contact face 2.2 mm2 at r 6.05; rib section 2.0 x 3.5 mm, lever 1.45 to the bore wall; tip at 53.75 mm.
- 3 N at the tip: 12.1 MPa bearing, 9.5 MPa bending.
- 7 N: 28.3 bearing, 22.1 bending.
- 10 N: 40.4 bearing, 31.5 bending (above UTS 29-32).
- A child pushing the arm back past -51 deg or up past +140.5 deg can easily apply 5-10 N. Homing alone is only 1.3 MPa.
issues.fix: Keep the same stop angles but widen the rib to about 90 deg and narrow the lug to about 78.5 deg (rib width + lug width = 168.5 deg). Increase the radial overlap to r 5.2..7.0. At 7 N this gives about 17 MPa bearing and 3 MPa bending; check the bore-wall root. Alternatively move the stop to a larger radius. Add an anti-rotation key for the arm hub in the T3 shell, because the homing reference depends on it.

issues.what: Voxel discretisation of the fill breaks two clearance rules. The judge specified an exact cut only for the coupler.
issues.evidence:
v_clear_L/R.json, measured at fill voxel corners:
- Servo slide-in corridor: 0.10 mm at (33.0, 9.0, -49.0) L and (-41.5, 9.0, -49.0) R. The rule is 0.30. Cause: voxel centres were excluded only up to y <= 9.2.
- Fill to the T_paluba edge: 0.126 mm at (31.0, 14.5, -48.0); 33 corners are below 0.3 (v_deck.json). The specified extra 'trim 0.1' still leaves less than 0.3.
- Other fill checks are fine: sweep 1.156 L / 1.148 R, T_stred lowering 0.60, cap removal 0.60, coupler corridor 0.50, lifted hex 2.19.
issues.fix: Build the fill in CAD from exact cutters, not voxels: y >= 9.2 / y <= -14.6 and x >= 32.65 cut for z < -44.5 (servo + 0.3); x >= 31.3 at the deck; the coupler cylinder r 5.0 and slab as already specified.

issues.what: The servo height conflict is still open and blocks freezing the CAD.
issues.evidence: The official SC09 drawing gives 25.25 mm to the top face; the v2 pocket used 21.5. With the top face held at -45, the bottom goes to -70.25. The relocated buck converter (x 19.85..37.65, top -70.95, g2.py BUCK) overlaps the servo footprint at x 32.95..37.65, leaving 0.70 mm for a pad that is 2.2 mm in v2. Raising the servo instead moves the spline, coupler, hex socket and shaft stack, which interacts with the axial issue above.
issues.fix: Measure the real servo. Then either move the buck converter or redesign the pocket floor, and freeze the coupler and shaft z-stack afterwards (together with the axial fix above).

issues.what: An inward push on the arm is carried only by the A2 balls and A2's epoxy bond. Nothing stops the gear from being pushed into the pinion.
issues.evidence: Load path: washer -> drive-hub pocket bottom on the M4 head -> M4 -> A2 inner race -> balls -> epoxied outer race. The backup gaps (rib to ring end 0.5, drive-hub boss to seat end 0.5) are far larger than the 0.088 backlash, and the gear moves with the M4, so the teeth jam before either gap closes (1.42 x the axial force as tooth normal load). The MR74 static axial capacity is about 0.5 C0 (judge C0 107 N, catalogues about 107-150 N), so roughly 55-75 N. A hand pressing the arm against the body can exceed that and brinell A2 (notchy, noisy drive).
issues.fix: Add an inward thrust stop that engages within the backlash budget: for example a PTFE washer between the drive-hub boss and the seat end face, gap set to about 0.05-0.08 by coupon or gauge. Alternatively state an explicit 'do not press the arm inward' warning and accept the risk.

issues.what: Shim and spacer diameters can touch the wrong bearing ring or the shields.
issues.evidence:
- Pinion shim r 1.55..1.9 (OD 3.8): the MR63 inner-ring land is about 3.8-4.0 mm, so the rotating shim can rub the shield.
- Gear shim r 2.05..2.9 (OD 5.8): it overhangs the MR74 shield zone (about r 2.5..3.0).
- Spacer sleeve D7/D5: its bore is at the MR74 inner-ring outside diameter (about 4.9-5.2 mm). It can touch the rotating inner rings, which would bypass the intended outer-race thrust path and add drag.
issues.fix: Pinion shim OD <= 3.6; gear shim OD <= 4.9; spacer bore >= 5.6 so it touches the outer races only.

issues.what: The MR63 inner race is a slip fit on a printed shaft that rotates against a mesh load fixed in direction, so it will creep.
issues.evidence: The mesh force direction is fixed in space while the shaft turns, so the inner race carries a rotating load on a 0.01-0.03 slip fit. That makes it roll on the resin journal (about pi x clearance per revolution) and fret it. The judge's argument that friction makes the race follow is about average rotation, not creep. Loads are small (radial 1.36 N at slip, about 0.3 N running), so slow wear is expected, not failure.
issues.fix: Use a light press (by coupon) of the D3 journal in the MR63 and keep the service lift (pull through), or accept the wear and list it as unverified.

issues.what: Some open concerns are relieved because the strength and play estimates used a 72 mm tip lever. The real tip distance is 53.75 mm.
issues.evidence:
- Plug seat under L5: 10 N x 53.75 mm = 538 N.mm on a D10/D5 section (Z 92 mm3) gives 5.8 MPa, 7.0 with Kt 1.2. That is below 8.5 (judge 7.8/9.4).
- Tilt play: 0.0101 rad x 53.75 = 0.54 mm (judge 0.73).
- Face-preload tilt threshold: 4.0-8.8 N of clamp (window / (mu x 7.7 mm)) gives about 0.75-1.6 N at the tip.
- Swing play from backlash: 1.04 deg, about 1.0 mm at the tip plus servo backlash.
issues.fix: Update the numbers in the user text. With the lever corrected, the plug seat is no longer an open overstress.

issues.what: The magnet count is probably 2-5, not 'typically 4-7'. Some force and friction combinations fit no integer count.
issues.evidence: v_magnet.py/json: image-method charge model of a 5x2 N38 magnet on an ideal plate, 3.6 N at a 0.25 mm gap and 3.05 N at 0.35 mm (the contact value is not converged and was not used). With a real-plate factor of 0.5-0.85, that is 1.5-3.0 N per magnet, or 0.0029-0.0092 N.m per magnet at r 7.7 with mu 0.25-0.4. 6 of the 18 F/mu combinations fit no integer count in 0.0124-0.0170 without spacers. With 2-3 magnets the layout in 8 pockets is asymmetric (uneven face pressure, tilt). Magnets must not be glued during tuning.
issues.fix: Tell the user to expect 2-4 magnets (opposite pairs first), not to glue them (the washer holds them against the skin), and to tune with spacers.

issues.what: Availability of some bought items is still unverified (rule b).
issues.evidence: 6700ZZ, MR63ZZ and the Loctite 638 activator (SF 7649) were not confirmed in SK/CZ shops; the session has no network and the judge relied on search snippets. The user's tool list has Loctite 638/222 but no activator.
issues.fix: Confirm the shops before freezing. Fallbacks: 2K epoxy instead of 638 + activator on the races; 6800ZZ (10x19x5, more common) with a hub re-check.

issues.what: Smaller durability and printing details.
issues.evidence:
- Plug M2 screws are only snug with no threadlocker and may loosen. 222 on the metal screw / brass insert interface is allowed.
- Support nubs on the pinion back-face land and 0.30 mm shims printed flat (burn-in layers) give a poor axial reference and thickness.
- The coupler and shaft run next to the servo (65 C limit); the Tough heat-deflection temperature and creep are unverified.
- Gravity torque crosses zero at the 0 deg rest pose, so the flanks flip across the backlash (soft click); the claim 'taken up silently' is optimistic.
- The T4 T_bok flange (x 39.0) overlaps the boss stop ring (x 38.4..39.1) by 0.1 in the meshes (v_clear static 0.0/0.001); this is an inherited designed contact, so confirm the v2 cap trim.
issues.fix: Allow 222 on the screws; put supports off the reference lands; measure the shims with calipers; list the heat and creep items as unverified; correct the noise text; confirm the cap flange trim.

checked: Rules (a)/(b)/(c): found no part that needs cutting, drilling, tapping, turning, grinding or bending of metal, and no catalogue-specialist part. DIN 912 M4x20 is fully threaded for M4 lengths up to 25 (ISO 4762), so it is used at stock length; screws are only picked by calipers; the trimmed horn and servo ears are plastic. Availability of 6700ZZ, MR63ZZ and the 638 activator is unverified (see the notes).

Bevel geometry and envelope, own calculation (v_gear.py): delta 33.690/56.310, R 7.2115, b/R 0.388, m at toe/mean 0.4078/0.5373. Pinion: crown r 4.499 at z -22.667, heel root -23.426, toe -20.467 r 2.752. Gear: toe x 41.142 r 3.874, crown 42.501 r 6.333, root 43.638. Identical to the judge.

Virtual spur teeth (my own rack generation, PA 25, ha 0.9, hf 1.15, rho 0.38): z_v 14.42/32.45; Y (tip direction) 0.3981/0.4982; Kf 1.405/1.550 at the minimum fillet radius; contact ratio 1.291; no undercut. Top land: toe 0.249 (pinion) / 0.274 (gear), heel 0.407/0.447. Root clearance 0.10 at the toe. Printable at 16K (about 14 um pixel, about 17 px on the toe top land).
Pinion forces at the 0.017 N.m slip: Ft 3.52 N, axial 0.91 N downward. So the mesh thrust does hold the pinion on its shim, radial 1.36 N. Gear axial thrust 1.36 N outboard.

Sweep clearance to pan +-90.3 / lift 0..20 (own exact azimuth formula and lift interval on mov.npz), L/R: coupler 1.231/1.601; pinion 1.232/1.617 (also with the 0.60 shim: 1.233/1.617); tongue 1.331/1.715; boss 1.016/1.396; MR63 >= 2.53; gear, M4, A1/A2 and spacer have no sample within 2.5; fill corners 1.156/1.148. All >= 1.0 (boss only just).
Static clearance to kept T4 parts, L = R: coupler 2.50, vertical shaft 0.505 (inside the v2 T_bok notch), pinion 3.40 (3.55 with the 0.60 shim), MR63 1.43, tongue 0.462, gear 5.27. All >= 0.3.

Fill paths, both sides: T_stred lowering 0.60, side-cap removal 0.60, coupler slide corridor 0.50, rotating coupler 0.50, servo output boss slide 1.0, lifted hex 2.19. The right fill does not overhang the deck (0 voxels).

Arm gap against the real T_bok_L and mirrored T_bok_P meshes plus the recessed plug disc (v_gap.json): rest 3.702, -45 deg 3.333, 130 deg 1.153, 135 deg 1.001, 140.5 deg 0.862. The two sides are identical and match the judge's analytic surface.

verification.verdict:
B1+ is not ready to print. What holds up: the rules on metal work and common parts are met. My own scripts reproduce the gear geometry (Y, Kf and contact ratio) and all clearances to the moving pan/lift parts (>= 1.0 on both sides). The arm gap of 3.70 at rest and 1.00 at +135 matches against the real side-cap mesh. What fails, four must-fix items:
(1) The coin calibration of the clutch cannot be done. The arm reaches only 53.75 mm from the axis, not 60, and its gravity torque is about 0.002 N.m, not 0.004.
(2) On the left, the merged column fill sits above the trimmed T_paluba deck (535 voxels at x 26-31, z -46..-43), so the deck can no longer be lowered into place.
(3) The column hand check leaves out the torsion from the off-axis tip load. With it, the back leg of the column alone reaches 10-27 MPa, so the claim of 5.1/7.15 MPa does not show the problem is fixed.
(4) The vertical shaft is located axially in more than one place: the shaft step, the pinion seat and the hex resting on the socket floor. The coupler height or the horn screw can lift the pinion off its shim and bind the mesh.
Should-fix items:
- The tooth margin at the clutch slip torque is zero, and 10.3 MPa with Km 1.25. Lower the clutch window.
- The form-radius margin is only 0.023 mm at the toe. Add tip relief.
- The pinion shim set covers far less than the tolerance stack.
- The arm gap is below 1.0 mm at the homing stop and has no margin at +135.
- The stop rib breaks at about 7 N of hand push at the arm tip.
- The voxelised fill leaves 0.10 mm to the servo slide path and 0.13 mm to the deck (rule 0.3).
- The servo height conflict (25.25 vs 21.5) is still open.
- An inward push on the arm loads only A2's balls and its epoxy.

final.winner: B1+ fixer revision (R2c/oprava). It is the judge's B1+: printed 12/18 bevel pair, DIN 912 M4x20 arm shaft, ball bearings, magnetic friction clutch, B2 column fill. All 23 verifier issues were reproduced and fixed, or reported as still open with numbers. One issue is NOT closed: under L5 the column alone is still above 8.5 MPa at +135 deg, so T_spodok is not released for printing. Changes: 6700ZZ replaced by a 6800ZZ/2RS arm bearing; gear ha* 0.8 tip relief; clutch window lowered to 0.0082-0.0113 N.m with a reachable coin test; defined vertical shaft stack (5 AF socket with a printed ledge, step at z -24.5); printed C-shim inward stop; 90 deg stop rib with stops at -51/+135.5 and working range -45..+130; per-position M2 screw lengths; epoxy instead of Loctite 638 + activator; column fill clipped exactly plus a new torsion web; honest availability labels.

RULES CHECK (a)/(b)/(c), part by part.
- No metal is cut, drilled, tapped, turned or ground. The washer burr is not sanded: the burr side is glued into the recess.
- Bought parts, all at stock size:

- (b) is NOT demonstrated for any bought part. WebSearch was refused because the shared budget of 200 searches was used up. WebFetch returned ENOTFOUND for www.loziska-policka.cz, www.laskakit.cz and umakov.cz in this session (the verifier saw the same for about 20 shop hosts). Every row is therefore labelled 'availability not confirmed'.
- The 6800 replaces the 6700 because 6800 (61800) is a standard catalogue size in general bearing ranges, while the 67xx thin series is mainly an RC size. This is a judgement, not a check.

WHY B1+ STAYS THE WINNER. The judge's ranking holds: ball bearings in every rotating joint, the horn/cup coupling, more tooth margin than B2, and a firm arm. The fixes below make the margins real.

FIXES (reproduced first, then re-checked with my scripts in /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/oprava):
(1) 6700 -> 6800ZZ/2RS (10x19x5) at x 55.3..60.3. The outer stack is squeezed back to x <= 67.55: flange 0.8, drive-hub disc 3.05, lip ring 0.8. Room left in the arm is 1.29..1.40 (hub_fix2.json). The 6800 without squeezing failed: 0.64 / 0.75. The 6700 hub stays as a drop-in fallback print.
(2) Gear ha* 0.9 -> 0.8 with tips rounded r 0.1. Contact ratio 1.291 -> 1.222. Toe margin between pinion form radius and SAP 0.023 -> 0.038 mm (backlash equivalent 0.064 -> 0.095, above the nominal 0.088).
(3) Clutch window 0.0124-0.0170 -> 0.0082-0.0113 N.m.
  * Pinion at the top of the window: 5.58 MPa (x Kf), 6.97 (x Kf x Km 1.25). Before: 8.25 / 10.31.
  * D-key 3.4 MPa (was 5.0).
  * The lower limit is still 2x the 0.004 running limit.
(4) Coin test redefined at a reachable radius.
  * Printed tip clip with the thread hole at R 55.0; arm torque 0.0016-0.0022 N.m (v_arm), not 0.004.
  * 2 EUR + 2 c must hold and 2 EUR + 50 c must slip: this checks a window of 0.0082-0.0113.
  * Symmetric magnet patterns 2/4/6/8 with printed spacers cover every per-magnet value from 0.0018 to 0.0092 N.m, so 8 pockets are enough.
(5) Vertical stack.
  * 5 AF socket with a printed ledge at z -38.4; the horn screw head sits in a recess below it.
  * D3->D2.5 step moved to z -24.5, which is >= 0.85 below the pinion for every shim.
  * The pinion height is now set only by the shim.
(6) Backlash.
  * Tooth-thickness coupon pairs.
  * Gear shim 0.20/0.30/0.40 chosen by a dry-fit depth measurement before bonding.
  * Pinion shims 0.22..0.57 in 0.05 steps, capped at 0.57 to protect the depth margin.
(7) Inward stop: a printed C-shim (0.45/0.47) in the 0.5 gap at the seat end. It engages before the 0.113 mm axial move that would jam the mesh, so pushes never reach A2's balls, A2's bond or the teeth.
(8) Two-sided stop.
  * Rib 90 deg (r 5.5..7.5), lug 83.5 deg (r 5.0..7.0, x 52.5..54.8); contacts at -51 / +135.5.
  * Working range -45..+130: arm gap 1.153 at the range end; rib-lug gap 0.576 at -45 and 0.528 at +130.
  * Stop bearing stress 22.3 MPa at a 7 N tip push (was 28.3 bearing / 22.1 bending).
(9) Plug screws.
  * DIN 965 M2x8 at 12 o'clock, M2x10 at 4 o'clock, M2x10 at 8 o'clock with the countersink 1.3 deeper.
  * The verifier's M2x12 at 8 o'clock would bottom on the insert-hole floor (x 34.9).
(10) Inner races bonded with 2K epoxy, so no activator is needed (Loctite 638 + 7649 optional).
(11) Washer: zinc-plated steel, not stainless; the burr side goes into the recess.
(12) M4: buy two packs, accept a major diameter >= 3.90 (3.93 preferred), size the drive-hub coupons from the measured head diameter.
(13) Column fill: clipped exactly at the deck path and the servo corridor. Deck static and path clearance 0.003 -> 0.30; servo slide 0.10 -> 0.45.
(14) Column torsion web added at z -35..-27 between the legs.
  * Voxel FE of the column alone halves the plug tilt and the boss and upper-leg stresses at 0 and 90 deg.
  * Still above 8.5 MPa at +135 and below the deck, so this item stays open and blocks printing.
(15) Shop codes with no saved evidence were removed. The horn is only a 'maybe in the box' item; the printed spline is a fully specified path.

  * both inner races bonded on the M4 thread with 2K epoxy.
- Arm shaft DIN 912 M4x20 (major diameter >= 3.93 preferred, >= 3.90 accepted):
  * shank x 40..60; head x 60..64;
  * head set 0.5 off the seat end with a printed gauge fork while curing;
  * gear shim between the gear back and A1.
- NEW inward stop: printed C-shim 0.45 or 0.47 (r 2.1..4.4, opening 4.2), clipped into the 0.5 gap between the seat end and the head / drive-hub boss after the cure (gap 0.03-0.05).
  * Inward loads (arm refit, pushes) go through the C-shim into the seat face, never through A2's balls or bond, and never into the teeth.
  * Outward gear thrust: A1 -> spacer -> A2 -> shoulder.

5 ARM SIDE (inside the arm, dx -1.0)
- Arm bearing 6800ZZ or 6800-2RS (10x19x5) at x 55.3..60.3.
  * Outer race epoxied in the hub bore D19; inner race slip on the D10 seat (4.2 of 5.0 supported).
  * Room left in the arm 1.29..1.40.
- Printed arm hub:
  * ring A r 7.5..8.8, x 53..55, carries the rib;
  * ring B r 7.5..10.7, x 54.5..55.3 (bearing shoulder);
  * bore wall r 9.5..10.7 to x 61.2;
  * flange 0.8 thick, x 60.4..61.2;
  * wall r 11.5..12.7 to x 67.55;
  * bonded lip ring 0.8, x 66.75..67.55, inner r 10.4.
- Rib: x 53..55, r 5.5..7.5, 90 deg wide, at azimuth 135..225 at rest.
- Washer DIN 125 M10, zinc-plated steel (NOT stainless), r 5.25..10, x 61.2..63.2.
  * The smooth burr-free face is the friction face, set flush to the reference (hub face down on glass).
  * The burr side goes into the recess; the epoxy takes the thickness tolerance.
- Drive hub (printed, captive):
  * pocket on the M4 head x 60..64, diameter = measured head diameter - 0.01/0.02/0.03 by coupon (knurled head: measure over the knurl);
  * hex 3 AF key;
  * boss r 3.5..4.5, x 60..63.2;
  * disc r 11.0, x 63.2..66.25, friction skin 0.25;
  * 8 pockets D5.1 at r 7.7, depth 2.8, open outboard.
- Clutch:
  * NdFeB 5x2 N38 axial magnets, alternating polarity, in symmetric patterns of 2/4/6/8;
  * printed spacers 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8 under the magnets (force x 0.72/0.54/0.41/0.33);
  * window 0.0082-0.0113 N.m at the arm.
- Coin test:
  * printed clip on the arm tip, thread hole on the arm axis at R 55.0 from the shoulder axis;
  * arm horizontal forward, servo holding;
  * 2 EUR + 2 c (11.56 g) must HOLD; 2 EUR + 50 c (16.30 g) must SLIP.
- Two-sided hidden stop: the rib meets the lug at -51.0 and +135.5. Rib-lug gap 0.576 at -45 and 0.528 at +130.
- Arm on/off: as B1+ (cover off, straight pull; refit at the hanging pose until the hex key drops in).
- Fallback: if only a 6700ZZ can be bought, print the judge's B1+ 6700 hub (bore D15, x 55.5..59.5).

6 FIRMWARE
- Running torque limit 15 %, 65 C.
- Working range -45..+130 (NEW). Limit acceleration so the dynamic torque stays <= 0.004 N.m.
- Homing at every power-up and after any unexpected load peak:
  1. slow sweep to the servo low end (the arm stops at -51, the clutch slips);
  2. slow sweep to the high end (the arm stops at +135.5, the clutch slips).
- Needs servo travel >= 284 deg (span 186.5 x 1.5 + margin; nominal 300).

7 ASSEMBLY
- Bench:
  1. Print the coupons: D3 in MR63, D7 bore, D10 seat with the 6800, 5 AF hex, spline, head press, skin, tooth pairs.
  2. Epoxy the MR63 into the tongue and the M2 inserts into the boss.
  3. Dry fit A2, spacer, A1, M4, gear shim and gear. Measure 3.24 and choose the gear shim.
  4. Epoxy A2 against the shoulder and let it cure; insert the spacer and A1.
  5. Insert the M4 with epoxy on the bearing zones and the 0.5 gauge under the head.
  6. Screw on the chosen shim and the gear with epoxy in the thread.
  7. After the cure: remove the gauge and clip in the C-shim.
- Torso:
  1. Shaft up through the MR63; pinion with the 0.42 shim on top.
  2. Lift the shaft 3.5.
  3. Slide the servo with its coupler (screw already driven) in along -X.
  4. Lower the shaft until the hex sits on the ledge.
  5. Fit the cap, then the plug (pegs, 3 screws snug, no threadlocker).
  6. Check the tip play and that nothing is tight; change the pinion shim if needed.
  7. Grease the teeth; fit the arm and the cover.
  8. Home, then do the coin test.
- Servo swap about 10 min, as before.

8 RIGHT SIDE
- Mirror x -> -x. Fill colfill_fix_R.npz uses the same clip and web rules. The web is the J1 cradle end wall, as in v2.
- FE R: p99.9 11.6-17.7, the same pattern as L.

Vytlač všetky diely, umy ich a vytvrď: spojka A alebo B, zvislý hriadeľ, pastorok, koleso so závitom M4, podložky, puzdro, C-podložky, zátka, unášač, náboj ruky, krúžok, rozpierky pod magnety, kaliber 0,5 a háčik na koniec ruky.
Servo: bočnými štípačkami odstrihni plastové úšká a zabrús ich.

Spojka A (ak je v balení páčka): odstrihni rameno páčky, pilníkom zapiluj dve plôšky na 6,2 mm a páčku vlep epoxidom do spojky. Spojka B: vyber kupón drážkovania. Spojku nasaď na servo a cez šesťhranný otvor zaskrutkuj skrutku M2 (DIN 912).

Vlep vonkajší krúžok MR63 do jazýčka v T_spodok a 3 mosadzné vložky M2 do nálitku (2K epoxid).

Zátka nasucho: vlož A2, puzdro, A1, skrutku M4, podložku pod koleso a koleso, zatiaľ bez lepidla. Hĺbkomerom zmeraj vzdialenosť od čela krčku zátky po čelo kolesa. Podľa toho vyber podložku 0,20 / 0,30 / 0,40 tak, aby vyšlo 3,24 mm. Potom všetko rozober.
Vonkajší krúžok MR74 (A2) vlep epoxidom do otvoru Ø7 až na doraz a nechaj vytvrdnúť. Potom vlož puzdro a A1.

Natri tenkú vrstvu 2K epoxidu na závit M4 v miestach ložísk. Zasuň skrutku zvonka a pod hlavu daj kaliber 0,5 mm. Z dutiny nasaď vybranú podložku a naskrutkuj koleso s epoxidom v závite. Drž, kým lepidlo stuhne.
Po vytvrdnutí vyber kaliber a do medzery pod hlavou zacvakni C-podložku 0,45 (alebo 0,47, ak tá ide voľne).
Náboj ruky: vlep ložisko 6800 vonkajším krúžkom. Podložku M10 odmasti a vlep hladkou stranou (bez otrepu) na sklo; stranu s otrepom daj do drážky a nič nebrús. Vlož unášač a nalep krúžok.
Magnety 5×2: over, že sú axiálne. Vlož 4 ks do protiľahlých vreciek unášača so striedavou polaritou (kvapka epoxidu).

Montáž v trupe: zvislý hriadeľ zasuň zdola cez MR63 a navrch daj pastorok s podložkou 0,42. Hriadeľ nadvihni o 3,5 mm, servo so spojkou zasuň pozdĺž −X a hriadeľ spusti, kým šesťhran nesadne na dno spojky. Nasaď bočný kryt.
Vlož zátku (2 kolíky do otvorov) a jemne dotiahni skrutky: hore M2×8, vľavo a vpravo dole M2×10 (pri 8. hodine je hlbšie zahĺbenie). Bez zaisťovača.
Ruku nasaď vo visiacej polohe, pootoč, kým šesťhranný kolík zapadne do hlavy skrutky, a rovno zatlač.

Kontrola vôle: servo drží, končekom ruky jemne kývaj. Vôľa má byť 0,9 – 2,0 mm a nikde v rozsahu nesmie drhnúť. Ak je vôľa malá, daj tenšiu podložku pod pastorok; ak je veľká, hrubšiu, ale najviac 0,57. Ak to nestačí, použi pár koliesok s hrubšími zubami.
Zuby natri PTFE tukom alebo grafitom (tuk najprv 3–7 dní vyskúšaj na odpadovom výtlačku). Trecie plochy spojky nechaj suché. Nasaď kryt ruky.
Firmvér: limit momentu 15 %, 65 °C, rozsah −45° až +130°. Nulovanie pri zapnutí: pomalý prechod dole (doraz −51°), potom hore (doraz +135,5°). Spojka sa vždy krátko prešmykne.

Kalibrácia spojky: ruka vodorovne dopredu, servo drží. Na koniec ruky nasaď tlačený háčik a na nite zaves zlepené mince. 2 € + 2 c musí držať, 2 € + 50 c sa musí prešmyknúť. Ak spojka drží slabo, pridaj magnety (2/4/6/8 súmerne); ak drží príliš silno, uber magnety alebo pod ne vlož rozpierky 0,2 – 0,8.
Pravá ruka rovnako (zrkadlovo). Skúšku mincami zopakuj raz ročne.
changes_vs_v2: Brass m0.5 16/24 bevel pair replaced by a PRINTED straight bevel pair 12/18, m 0.6667, PA 25: pinion ha* 0.9, gear ha* 0.8 (fixer tip relief), tips r 0.1, b 2.8. Same apex and ratio. Contact ratio 1.222.
Steel D3 vertical shaft with a D-flat replaced by a printed shaft: hex 5 AF / D3 / D2.5 D-key. The step is at z -24.5, so the pinion height is set only by its shim (fixer).

Brass coupler sleeve and grub screw replaced by a printed cup with a 5 AF socket on a printed ledge and a head recess. Path A: trimmed horn bonded in. Path B: printed 20T spline. Screw DIN 912 M2 (fixer: both paths fully specified).
Turned D4/D3 steel arm shaft replaced by a stock DIN 912 M4x20. The MR74 inner races are bonded with 2K epoxy (fixer: no Loctite activator). A2's outer race is epoxied against the shoulder (judge).
Gear: printed M4 internal thread, flank-centred (judge). Its shim is chosen by a dry-fit depth measurement before bonding (fixer).
NEW printed C-shim inward stop at the seat end (fixer): arm pushes never reach A2 or the teeth.

Disc-spring clutch replaced by a magnetic friction clutch (5x2 magnets in a printed drive hub against a DIN 125 M10 zinc steel washer). Fixer window 0.0082-0.0113 N.m, symmetric magnet patterns plus printed spacers. Coin test with a printed tip clip at R 55: 2 EUR + 2 c holds, 2 EUR + 50 c slips.
Arm retention: the drive hub is pressed onto the M4 head, with coupons sized from the measured head diameter (fixer), plus a printed hex key.
Homing: two-sided hidden stop. Rib 90 deg vs lug 83.5 deg, contacts at -51 / +135.5 (fixer). Two slow sweeps at the running limit.
Working range -45..+135 reduced to -45..+130 (fixer): arm gap 1.15 at the range end, 0.99 only at the hidden homing stop.
6700 moved outboard (B1), then replaced by 6800ZZ/2RS 10x19x5 at x 55.3..60.3 with a squeezed outer stack: flange 0.8, disc 3.05, lip 0.8 (fixer). The 6700 hub stays as a fallback print.
D2 h6 dowels replaced by printed D2.4 pegs. Plug and boss slots |y-3| <= 5.1. Plug screws DIN 965 M2x8 / M2x10 / M2x10 with a 1.3 deeper countersink (fixer).

Column: steel rods removed. B2 upper fill clipped exactly to the deck path and the servo corridor (fixer). NEW torsion web between the legs at z -35..-27 (fixer). Fillets R >= 1.0 at the pocket corners.
PORON strips replaced by optional felt tape.
Firmware: running limit 15 % (v2 allowed up to 30 %), 65 C, range -45..+130.
torso_parts_to_reprint: T_paluba: v2 trim (left lobe x <= 31.0 except the r 3.15 lobe around F3a_2). The judge's extra 0.1 trim is no longer needed: the fill now keeps 0.30 to the deck and its lowering path.
T_bok_L and T_bok_P: v2 inner notch x +-39.0..41.2, |y-3| <= 2.0, z -33.5..-27.5. Exterior unchanged.
Arm side, not torso: printed 6800 arm hub and 0.8 lip ring bonded into the T3 arm shell (shell geometry unchanged); printed drive hub; printed coin tip clip.
final.arm_gap:
Unchanged look: no visible part moves.
- Plug face recessed 1.0 in the r 14 socket. Black D13 ring into the arm's D14 hole. Arm at dx -1.0.
- Gap along the swing (the judge's rec1 numbers and the verifier's v_gap agree):
  * 3.70 at rest (cap rim near (49.3, 1.5, -30.9));
  * 3.33 at -45;
  * 1.53 at +120;
  * 1.153 at +130, the NEW working-range end.
- Homing only: 0.99 at the hidden top stop +135.5 (0.947 at +137 for reference). The arm stops there on the rib and never touches the torso.
- Axial stack: plug shoulder -> bonded A2 (+-0.025) -> M4 head set with the 0.5 gauge (+-0.03) -> drive-hub pocket (+-0.03) -> washer face referenced flush. That is about +-0.08: +130 gives 1.07-1.23 and the stop gives 0.91-1.07.
- The C-shim limits inward travel to 0.03-0.05.
- Under a hand push the bearing and seat tilt play closes the gap by about 0.14 more (verifier estimate). That is an abuse case, not motion.
- Check after assembly: arm skin to plug face on the axis 3.9 +- 0.1. Correct it with the drive-hub pocket depth, not with the gear shim.
final.noise:
* **Gear mesh.** One added mesh: a greased resin straight bevel pair.
  * At most about 0.25-0.75 rev/s at the pinion, so a 3-9 Hz mesh frequency and no tonal whine.
  * The gear tip relief (ha* 0.8, r 0.1 tips) softens tip entry.
  * The SCS0009's own metal gear train stays the dominant sound.
* **Bearings.** Every rotating joint runs on greased ball bearings (MR63, 2x MR74, 6800). No dry resin journals.
* **Clutch.**
  * Silent in running.
  * At every power-up homing it scrapes twice, softly, without detents: up to about 7 deg of slip at the arm at each hidden stop.
  * The lower window (0.0082-0.0113 N.m) makes the slip quieter than in B1+.
* **No rattle.**
  * The pinion is held by its own thrust; the shaft now sits on a printed ledge, not on the screw head.
  * The C-shim has only a 0.03-0.05 gap and carries no load in running.
  * The drive hub is pressed on; felt tape on the servo pocket is optional.
* Noise was not measured. This is a qualitative estimate.
final.durability:
**Teeth** (fixer window, gear ha* 0.8):
- Running 0.004 N.m: 1.94 MPa (x Kf), 2.43 (x Kf x Km 1.25).
- Running 0.008 N.m: 3.88 / 4.85, below the 6 MPa cyclic target.
- Slip at the window top 0.0113 N.m: 5.58 / 6.97 MPa, below 8.5 with the AGMA load-distribution factor.
- Homing slips at every power-up, so they are not rare. At a few per day they add up to about 1e4 over years, still below 8.5.
- Wear is unverified. B1's Archard estimate (k 1e-5, +-10x) is 0.3-1.5 deg of extra backlash per 1e7 engagements.
- The pinion wears first. Swap: plug out (3 screws), new pinion on the D-key; about 15 min plus printing.
- The gear is replaced with a new M4x20 and a new plug print, because A2 is bonded.

**Creep.** No resin part carries a permanent preload.
- The clutch force is magnetic and closes internally.
- The plug screws are snug only.
- The C-shim is unloaded in running.
- The drive-hub press fit relaxes; this lowers only the breakaway force. Reprint the hub 0.01 tighter if needed (maximum 0.03).

**Clutch.**
- Face pressure about 0.04 MPa; about 1-2 mm of sliding per homing slip. Wear is negligible.
- If the skin wears, the magnet force rises, so the slip torque drifts up, not down. The annual coin test catches it; take away a magnet or add a spacer.

**Bearings.** MR63, MR74 and 6800 run far below their ratings.
- Inward pushes go to the C-shim, so the MR74 balls are not brinelled.
- The 6800 inner race only slides axially at arm fitting.

**Stops.** 90 deg rib, contact 2.7 mm2 at r 6.25.
- 0.67 MPa at homing.
- 9.6 MPa at a 3 N tip push; 22.3 MPa at 7 N.
- 31.9 MPa at 10 N: a local dent, no fracture (rib shear <= 3.9 MPa). The arm hub is a cheap reprint.

**Print drift.** Coupons are needed for:
- D3 in the MR63, the D7 bore, the D10 seat with the 6800;
- the 5 AF hex, the spline, the head press, the 0.25 skin;
- the tooth thickness (20 um layers).
final.strength:
Allowable 8.5 MPa long term. Fixer scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/gapwf/fin/R2c/oprava.

**Teeth** (gear_fix_ha0.80.json):
- Pinion tip-direction Lewis Y 0.398, Kf 1.405; gear Y 0.537, Kf 1.607.
- At 0.004: pinion 1.94 (x Kf) / 2.43 (x Kf x Km 1.25).
- At 0.008: 3.88 / 4.85.
- At the window top 0.0113-0.0115: pinion 5.58 / 6.97, gear 4.73.
- Allowable arm torque: 0.0175 (Kf), 0.0140 (Km 1.25), 0.0117 (Km 1.5). The window top is below all of them.

**Vertical drive** at 0.0115:
- D-key torsion 3.4 MPa (shear allowable 4.9).
- D3 bending at the MR63 3.1 MPa.
- Hex and spline below 1 MPa.

**Arm shaft and joints:**
- M4 bending under a sideways push 36 MPa (steel, B1).
- Inner-race epoxy about 0.4 MPa.
- C-shim: 50 N inward gives 0.85 MPa on the seat end face.
- The A2 bond carries no inward load any more.
- Outward pull at arm removal (14-22 N): A2's outer race presses on the shoulder.
- Drive-hub pocket edge 5.1 MPa; hex key 1.2 MPa (B1).

**Stop:** see durability (9.6 / 22.3 MPa bearing at a 3 / 7 N tip push).

**Plug seat under L5:** 7.8 MPa (9.4 with Kt 1.2), as in v2. FE pending.

**Column under L5** (10 N along X at the 53.75 mm tip; fe_col.py voxel FE h 0.5, column ALONE, stiff plug tied at the stop ring and screws, base fixed; values p99 / p99.9 / peak MPa):
- Judge fill, left:
  * 0 deg: legs 9.2/19.9/43.7, boss 8.6/19.1/37.3, tilt 27 mrad;
  * 90 deg: legs 8.7/17.0/39.1, below deck 8.5/11.8/22.8, boss 13.2/30.4/51.3;
  * 135 deg: legs 11.7/24.4/49.1 (not converged).
- With the NEW web, left:
  * 0 deg: legs 5.4/11.2/22.1, boss 5.0/6.9/11.9, tilt 15 mrad;
  * 90 deg: legs 6.4/11.6/26.0, below deck 7.7/10.7/19.5, boss 5.9/12.5/21.0;
  * 135 deg: legs 7.9/16.1/30.0, below deck 10.0/15.4/32.8, tilt 39 mrad.
- With the NEW web, right: 90 deg 6.8/12.7/27.5 and below deck 8.9/12.6/23.0; 135 deg legs 8.6/17.7/33.3 and below deck 11.1/16.1/27.3.
- Cable slot filled (left, 90 deg): below deck p99.9 10.7 -> 9.4.
- Plug neck bearing on the boss face: no gain (10.1 vs 11.2).
- Peaks sit at sharp voxel corners (pocket/pad corner, cable slot, stop-ring tie edge).

**Verdict:** the web is needed and roughly halves the upper-column stresses. The column alone still exceeds 8.5 at +135, mainly in the C-channel below the deck. The judge's 5.10 / 7.15 hand check is not a valid column result. Release T_spodok only after a CAD FE (fillets, real servo height, deck tie through F3a_2, T_bok flange in the clamp) shows <= 8.5.
final.summary_sk:
Prepracoval som víťazný návrh B1+ podľa všetkých výhrad overovateľov. Všetky som zopakoval vlastnými výpočtami a opravil najmenšou možnou zmenou. Nikde sa nereže ani nevŕta kov. Hlavné zmeny:
- ložisko 6700 nahradilo bežnejšie 6800 (10×19×5), ktoré sa po zúžení dielov zmestí do ruky;
- koleso má skrátené zuby, takže nastavovanie vôle už nemôže zatlačiť špičku zuba do pätky pastorka;
- prešmykový moment spojky je nižší (0,0082–0,0113 N·m), takže zuby majú rezervu aj s prísnym koeficientom (7,0 MPa pri dovolených 8,5).
Kalibrácia mincami sa teraz dá naozaj urobiť: na koniec ruky nasadíš tlačený háčik, 2 € + 2 c musí držať a 2 € + 50 c sa musí prešmyknúť. Zvislý hriadeľ sedí na tlačenom dne spojky, takže výšku pastorka určuje už len podložka. Pribudla tlačená C-podložka, ktorá zachytí zatlačenie ruky smerom k telu, aby nešlo do ložiska ani do zubov. Doraz v ruke je teraz široký 90°, takže sa pri silnom zatlačení skôr otlačí, ako zlomí. Pracovný rozsah je −45° až +130°, aby medzera k telu ostala aspoň 1 mm. Výplň stĺpa už neprekáža pri vkladaní paluby ani serva a pribudla priečka medzi nohami stĺpa.
Neoverené ostáva:
- Pevnosť stĺpa: môj výpočet MKP samotného stĺpa pri záťaži L5 je stále nad dovoleným napätím, preto T_spodok zatiaľ netlač.
- Dostupnosť dielov: stránky obchodov sa nedali otvoriť, takže pri žiadnom kupovanom diele nie je overené, že je skladom v SK/CZ.
- Výška serva: treba ju odmerať pred tlačou.
- Rozsah serva aspoň 284°.
- Životnosť tlačených zubov.
open_items: BLOCKING: column strength under L5. Column-alone voxel FE with the new web is still above 8.5 MPa at +135 deg: p99.9 15-18, p99 10-11 below the deck, peaks 27-33 at sharp corners. Do not print T_spodok until a CAD-based FE passes, with R >= 1.0 fillets, the real servo height and pad, the deck tie through F3a_2 (and any added deck screw) and the T_bok seat flange in the clamp. If it still fails, the next steps are tying the column foot and web to the deck, and moving the cable slot out of the front-leg foot (worth about -1.3 MPa).

BLOCKING for buying: availability. WebSearch budget used up; WebFetch ENOTFOUND for www.loziska-policka.cz, www.laskakit.cz and umakov.cz (verifier: about 20 shop hosts blocked). Allow the shop hosts in the session's network settings, or open the pages by hand. Re-check each row; mark 'in stock' only with a shop URL. MR74ZZ is the most likely mail-order item; 6800 vs 6700 is chosen by what a shop actually has (both hub prints exist).

Servo height and spline: the drawing gives 25.25 to the top face (bottom -70.25) vs the v2 pocket 21.5. The buck converter top at -70.95 leaves 0.70 for a 2.2 pad, so the buck converter must move or the pocket floor must be redesigned. The coupler stack is referenced to the measured servo top and horn hub, and the spline thread (M2?) must be confirmed before choosing the DIN 912 M2 length.
Servo travel must be >= 284 deg for the two-stop homing (span -51..+135.5). Check on the bench; if shorter, lower the top stop and the range end together (lug3.py).

Endurance test of a printed 12/18 pair (gear ha* 0.8): 1e4-1e5 moves at the clutch torque, backlash checked every 1e4. Grease compatibility with Tough on scrap for 3-7 days. No MSLA Tough gear wear data exists.

Real magnet force through the 0.25 skin and the friction coefficient on the zinc washer (estimates 0.0018-0.0092 N.m per magnet). Settled by the coin test; the arm shell mass (11-15 g assumed) and the clip mass (0.6 g estimate) should be weighed if a scale is available.
Drive-hub press fit on the M4 head (plain or knurled): retention and relaxation not measured; coupons from the measured head diameter.
Tooth geometry checked as 2-D virtual spur gears only (Lewis, Kf, contact ratio 1.222, form vs SAP 0.038 mm at the toe). No 3-D mesh or transmission-error check.
Elegoo Tough data (E about 2 GPa, UTS 29-32 MPa) comes from listings, not a TDS. No creep or fatigue data.
Plug seat D10 under L5: 7.8-9.4 MPa by hand. Include it in the CAD FE.
SC09 cable exit end decides which leg gets the cable slot. Keep the slot out of the leg foot and give its corners R >= 1.0.
